inspire.title: The Lot Falls on Yunus
inspire.content:
## Prophet Yunus (AS) Part - 4

 The Lot Falls on Yunus

The ship tossed violently in the storm as everyone gathered to draw lots. The process was simple: names would be drawn, and whoever's name came up would be identified as the one responsible for bringing this disaster upon them.

Yunus stood among them, his heart heavy with the knowledge of what was about to happen.

They drew the first lot.

The name that came up was: Yunus.

The people looked at him in shock and anger. "You! You're the reason we're in this storm!"

But wait - maybe it was a mistake? Maybe they should draw again just to be sure?

So they drew lots a second time.

Again, the name was: Yunus.

This was no coincidence. But the people were still uncertain. "Let's draw one more time to be absolutely certain!"

They drew lots a third time.

Once again: Yunus.

Three times! There could be no doubt now. According to their tradition, this man Yunus was the cause of the storm!

The people surrounded him, confused and angry. "Who are you? What have you done? Why has this disaster come upon us because of you?"

Yunus looked at their frightened faces. He could have lied. He could have tried to save himself. But he was still a prophet, and prophets speak the truth.

He took a deep breath and said: "I am a servant of Allah. I was sent as a messenger to my people, but I left them without permission from my Lord. This storm - it is because of me! I ran away from the responsibility Allah gave me!"

The people were amazed and terrified. A prophet? A messenger of God? And he had run away from his mission?

"Then what should we do?" they asked.

Yunus knew what had to happen. He could see it clearly now - this whole situation was Allah's way of stopping him, of making him face what he had done.

"Throw me into the sea," Yunus said calmly. "When I am gone, the storm will stop, and you will be safe."

But the sailors were not cruel men. They didn't want to throw someone into the raging sea to die!

"No!" the captain said. "We won't do that! We'll try to row to shore instead!"

So the sailors picked up their oars and rowed with all their strength, fighting against the powerful waves, trying desperately to reach land and safety.

They rowed and rowed, their muscles burning, sweat mixing with the rain pouring down on them. But it was useless! The storm was too strong! Every time they made a little progress, a huge wave would push them back!

The ship was sinking lower and lower. Water was filling it faster now. Time was running out!

Yunus spoke again, louder this time: "Listen to me! There is no other way! You must throw me into the sea! This is the only way you'll survive! This is what must happen!"

The sailors looked at each other, then at the sinking ship, then at the terrifying waves. They had tried everything else. Nothing had worked.

Finally, with heavy hearts and tears in their eyes, they agreed.

"We are sorry!" they cried out. "Forgive us! We don't want to do this, but we have no choice!"

Several men grabbed Yunus - gently, reluctantly - and carried him to the edge of the ship.

Yunus looked out at the dark, violent sea. The waves were enormous, like moving mountains of water. The storm raged with incredible fury. To fall into that sea was certain death!

But Yunus had accepted his fate. He understood now that this was his test, his consequence for running away. He had to face it.

Taking a deep breath, with the crew members' hands on his shoulders, Yunus closed his eyes...

And then they released him.

Yunus fell from the ship into the churning, dark waters of the sea!

## Lessons Learned:
- The truth always comes out - Yunus couldn't hide what he had done
- Accepting responsibility for our mistakes is the right thing to do, even when it's scary
- Not all people are cruel - the sailors didn't want to hurt Yunus and tried other solutions first
- Sometimes the consequences of our actions are severe, but we must face them with courage
- Allah's plans work in mysterious ways - what seemed like a disaster was actually part of the solution

**Reminder:** When you do something wrong, it's better to admit it and accept the consequences than to hide or run away. Yunus could have lied, but he told the truth. That's the behavior of a prophet - and that's how we should behave too!

inspire.title: Swallowed by the Whale
inspire.content:
## Prophet Yunus (AS) Part - 5

 Swallowed by the Whale

The moment Yunus hit the water, the sea swallowed him up. The waves crashed over him, pulling him down, down, down into the darkness.

But then, something miraculous happened!

The very moment Yunus entered the water, the storm stopped! Just like that - as if someone had flipped a switch! The howling wind became calm. The violent waves settled into gentle ripples. The dark clouds parted, and the sun began to shine through!

On the ship, the sailors stood in amazed silence, looking at the suddenly peaceful sea. Their lives had been saved! The prophet had been right!

But what about Yunus? Was he drowning in the sea?

No! Allah had a different plan for him - a plan so extraordinary, so unique, that nothing like it had ever happened before or since!

As Yunus sank deeper into the water, struggling, unable to breathe, Allah sent a huge creature from the depths of the ocean - a whale! But this was no ordinary whale. It was enormous, one of the biggest creatures in all of Allah's creation!

By Allah's command, this massive whale swam toward Yunus with its mouth wide open. And then - it swallowed him whole!

In one gulp, Yunus was inside the belly of the whale!

Can you imagine? One moment he was in the water, and the next moment he was inside a living creature, in complete darkness!

But here's the amazing part: Allah commanded the whale, "Do not break his bones or tear his flesh!" The whale was not to harm Yunus at all. It was simply to be a prison for him, a place where he would stay and think about what he had done.

So there was Yunus - alive, but trapped inside the belly of a whale, in the darkness of the sea!

It was completely dark. He couldn't see anything - not his hands, not anything at all. It was the darkest darkness imaginable!

First, there was the darkness of the night (for this happened at night).
Second, there was the darkness of the deep sea.
Third, there was the darkness inside the belly of the whale.

Three layers of darkness! The Quran describes it beautifully: "And [remember] the man of the fish (Yunus), when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses..." (Quran 21:87)

Yunus was in a place where no human had ever been before. He was in a situation that seemed completely hopeless. If anyone had a right to despair, it was Yunus!

But you know what? Yunus didn't despair. He didn't give up. He didn't curse his fate or blame Allah.

Instead, something amazing happened in that dark, lonely place. Yunus had a realization - a clear, powerful understanding of what he had done and what he needed to do.

He realized: "I ran away from my duty. I left the people I was sent to guide. I made a decision without consulting Allah. I let my frustration control me instead of trusting in Allah's plan. This situation I'm in - it's because of my own mistake!"

And in that moment of complete helplessness, in total darkness, unable to do anything for himself, Yunus did the only thing he could do.

He turned to Allah.

He began to pray.

## Lessons Learned:
- Allah has power over all His creation - He commanded the whale to swallow Yunus but not harm him
- Sometimes Allah puts us in difficult situations to make us think and realize our mistakes
- Even in the darkest, most hopeless situations, there is always hope in Allah
- Being alone and in difficulty can be a blessing - it makes us think deeply about our lives
- The first step to fixing a problem is recognizing and admitting that we made a mistake

**Reminder:** When you feel like you're in a dark place - maybe you're sad, or in trouble, or feeling alone - remember Yunus! If he could find hope in the belly of a whale in the deep, dark sea, then you can find hope in whatever difficulty you're facing! Allah is always there, always listening, always ready to help!

inspire.title: The Prayer in the Darkness
inspire.content:
## Prophet Yunus (AS) Part - 6 

In the belly of the whale, Yunus realized he had no one to turn to except Allah. With complete humility and sincere regret, Yunus called out:

"La ilaha illa Anta, Subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimeen!"

("There is no god except You! Glory be to You! Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers!")

This prayer contains three important things: belief in One God, glorifying Allah, and admitting mistakes. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that no Muslim ever prays with this supplication except that Allah answers their prayer!

Yunus repeated this prayer again and again with tears, hope, and faith. And Allah heard him! The Quran tells us: "And his Lord responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers!"

This beautiful prayer became a lesson for all believers throughout history - when we turn to Allah with sincere repentance, He forgives us and helps us!

## Prophet Yunus (AS) Part - 7 

After Yunus prayed his sincere prayer, Allah commanded the whale to swim toward the shore. When it reached the beach, the whale gently released Yunus onto the sand! He was alive! Allah had saved him!

But after spending so long in the belly of the whale, Yunus was very weak and sick. Allah's mercy continued - He caused a special gourd plant to grow right over Yunus! This plant had large leaves that provided shade, its fruit was nutritious, and it helped heal his skin.

As Yunus rested and recovered under the plant, he had time to reflect on everything that had happened. He realized that Allah had been teaching him important lessons about patience, not giving up on people, and trusting Allah's plan.

When Yunus had recovered his strength, Allah gave him a new command: "Go back to Nineveh!" This time, Yunus didn't hesitate. With humility and determination, he began the journey back to his people.

inspire.title: The Second Chance
inspire.content:
## Prophet Yunus (AS) Part - 8 

When Yunus approached Nineveh, he couldn't believe his eyes! The city was still standing and hadn't been destroyed! But something had changed dramatically.

After Yunus left, signs of Allah's punishment had appeared over Nineveh - dark, frightening clouds and terrifying sky colors. The people realized: "Yunus was telling the truth! The punishment is coming!"

In their terror and desperation, something extraordinary happened - the entire city, all hundred thousand people or more, came together to repent! Men, women, children, even their animals gathered in an open area. They cried out to Allah together:

"O Allah! We were wrong! We were foolish! Yunus was right, and we didn't listen! Please forgive us! We believe in You alone!"

It was the most sincere, massive repentance ever witnessed! And Allah accepted their repentance! The frightening clouds disappeared, and the city was saved. The people of Nineveh became believers - the only city in history where everyone believed together!

## Prophet Yunus (AS) Part - 9 

When Yunus entered Nineveh, he saw people praying and worshipping Allah alone! The people recognized him and rushed forward joyfully. "O Prophet Yunus! You were right! We were foolish not to listen to you! After you left, we saw the signs of punishment and repented, and Allah forgave us!"

Yunus was filled with joy, amazement, and humility. He understood now why Allah had put him through that whole experience: "Don't give up on people! You never know when they might turn to Me! Your job is to keep calling them to the truth and be patient. The results are in My hands, not yours!"

From that day forward, Yunus lived among the people of Nineveh, teaching them about Allah and guiding them. The city became a blessed place where everyone worshipped Allah and treated each other well.

Yunus's story became famous forever, teaching us that it's never too late to repent, never give up on people, and always trust Allah's wisdom and timing.

inspire.title: The Eternal Lessons from Yunus's Story
inspire.content:
## Prophet Yunus (AS) Part - 10 

The story of Prophet Yunus teaches us eternal lessons for our lives:

**The Power of Sincere Prayer**: Yunus's prayer "La ilaha illa Anta, Subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimeen" is one of the most powerful prayers. When we pray with this attitude - acknowledging Allah's power, praising Him, and admitting our faults - Allah answers our prayers!

**It's Never Too Late**: As long as you're alive, you can turn to Allah and He will forgive you. Allah loves to forgive and loves when His servants return to Him!

**Don't Give Up on People**: Yunus thought the people would never change, but he was wrong! Never give up on anyone - keep being kind, being a good example, and praying for them.

**Patience is Essential**: You can't expect everyone to change overnight. Sometimes it takes years, but you have to keep trying and trust Allah's timing.

**Learn from Mistakes**: Our mistakes can become our greatest teachers. When you make mistakes, don't despair - learn from them, repent, and become better!

**Trust Allah's Plan**: When things don't go the way you wanted, remember that Allah knows what you don't know. His plans are always better than ours!

inspire.title: The Righteous Family of Imran
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 1 

Long ago, there lived a very special family. The father's name was Imran, and he was a righteous, God-fearing man who served in the great temple in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). His wife, Hannah, was equally devoted to Allah.

They had been married for many years, but they had no children. This made Hannah very sad. She would see other women with their babies and pray to Allah: "O Allah, please bless me with a child!"

One day, as Hannah sat under a tree, she saw a bird feeding her babies. The mother bird put food into each baby bird's mouth with such love and care. This touched Hannah's heart deeply.

She raised her hands to the sky and made a special promise to Allah: "My Lord, I vow to You that if You give me a child, I will dedicate that child completely to Your service in the temple! The child will spend their life worshipping You and serving Your house. Please accept this from me. You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

It was a beautiful, sincere prayer from a pure heart.

And Allah answered her prayer! Hannah became pregnant! She was overjoyed! Every day of her pregnancy, she thanked Allah and prepared herself to fulfill her vow.

In those days, it was customary for families to dedicate their sons to serve in the temple. These boys would grow up learning the scriptures, worshipping Allah, and helping maintain the sacred place. It was considered a great honor.

Hannah was certain Allah would give her a son whom she would dedicate to His service, just as she had promised.

But when the time came for her to give birth, something unexpected happened. She delivered a baby girl!

Hannah held her newborn daughter in her arms - tiny, beautiful, and perfect. But she also felt confused. In that society, only boys were accepted for temple service. Girls were not allowed to stay in the temple dedicated to worship.

Hannah looked at her baby and said honestly: "My Lord, I have given birth to a female." She wasn't complaining - she was just stating the situation to Allah, knowing He already knew everything.

Then she said something very important: "And the male is not like the female."

She wasn't saying one was better than the other. She was saying they were different. Boys could fulfill temple service as she had planned, but what about a girl?

Despite her initial surprise, Hannah kept her promise to Allah. She said: "I have named her Maryam (Mary), and I seek Your protection for her and her descendants from Shaytan, the rejected one."

What a beautiful prayer! She asked Allah to protect her daughter and all her future children from the whispers and evil of Shaytan!

And Allah accepted Hannah's prayer! The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) told us that Maryam and her son Isa (Jesus) were the only people who were not touched by Shaytan when they were born. Every other human child cries at birth because Shaytan touches them, but not these two blessed individuals!

Allah said in the Quran: "So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner."

Even though Maryam was a girl, Allah had special plans for her - plans greater than anyone could have imagined!

inspire.title: The Little Girl in the Temple
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 2 

After Maryam was born, her mother Hannah wanted to fulfill her vow to Allah. She wanted to dedicate Maryam to serve in the temple, even though Maryam was a girl and this was not the custom.

Hannah wrapped baby Maryam warmly and brought her to the priests at the temple in Jerusalem. "I have vowed this child to Allah's service," she explained. "Please accept her."

The priests were surprised! A baby girl for temple service? This had never happened before!

But there was something special about this baby. Everyone who saw little Maryam felt drawn to her. There was a light about her, a purity, a blessing. The priests could sense that she was no ordinary child.

Word spread quickly among the religious leaders. Many of them wanted the honor of taking care of this special child!

You see, Maryam's family was well-respected. Her father Imran had been a righteous man (though he had passed away before Maryam was born), and everyone knew about Hannah's sincere vow.

The priests began to argue among themselves: "I should be her guardian!" "No, I am more qualified!" "I am older and wiser!" "I have more experience!"

They couldn't agree on who should take care of baby Maryam. Finally, someone suggested: "Let's draw lots! We'll write our names and put them in the river. Whoever's name stays afloat, that person will be Maryam's guardian!"

So they took their pens (which they used for writing scripture) and threw them into the river. All the pens sank except one - the pen belonging to a man named Zakariya (Zachariah)!

Zakariya was a prophet of Allah! He was elderly, very righteous, and wise. He was also Maryam's relative - married to her aunt. Allah chose him to be Maryam's guardian and teacher.

Zakariya was overjoyed! He took little Maryam under his care with great love and dedication. He built a special room for her in the temple - a private chamber called the "mihrab" where she could worship Allah in peace and privacy.

As Maryam grew from a baby to a little girl, and from a little girl to a young woman, Zakariya taught her everything: How to worship Allah properly, how to read and understand the scriptures, how to pray with devotion, how to be patient and grateful, and how to live a pure and righteous life.

Maryam was an exceptional student! She loved learning about Allah. She spent hours in prayer. She fasted often. She was humble, modest, and devoted completely to worshipping Allah.

She grew up isolated from the world, protected in the sacred temple, with her heart attached only to Allah. While other girls her age were playing and socializing, Maryam was praying and reading scripture.

She never complained. She never asked for luxuries. She was content with simple food and simple clothes. Her only desire was to please Allah.

The Quran tells us: "So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner, and put her in the care of Zakariya."

Zakariya watched Maryam grow with amazement and joy. He had never seen anyone so young be so devoted to Allah! She reminded him that true faith has no age limit - even a young person can have a heart full of love for Allah.

inspire.title: The Miracle of the Food
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 3 

As Maryam grew older in the temple under Zakariya's care, something miraculous began to happen - something that amazed even the prophet who was looking after her!

Zakariya would visit Maryam regularly in her private chamber (mihrab) to check on her, bring her food, and see if she needed anything. She spent most of her time there in worship and prayer, away from people's eyes.

One day, when Zakariya entered her room, he saw something that made him stop in his tracks. There was food in front of Maryam - fresh, delicious fruit! But this wasn't the food he had brought her. This was different!

Even more surprising, some of it was fruit that was out of season! In the winter, there were summer fruits. In the summer, there were winter fruits! This was impossible by normal means!

"O Maryam!" Zakariya exclaimed in wonder. "Where did you get this from?"

Maryam looked at him calmly and said simply: "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without measure."

Her answer was so simple, so full of faith! She didn't act amazed or proud. To her, it was completely natural - if you dedicate yourself to Allah, He takes care of you in ways beyond imagination!

This happened not just once, but repeatedly! Every time Zakariya came to visit her, he would find fresh provisions that he hadn't brought - fruits, food, sustenance appearing from nowhere!

It was a miracle! Allah was sending food directly to Maryam because of her sincere devotion and pure worship!

This miracle had a profound effect on Zakariya. Here he was, an old prophet who had served Allah for many years, and yet he had never received such obvious, continuous miracles. But this young woman, through her pure devotion, was being blessed in extraordinary ways!

Seeing Maryam's blessings made Zakariya think about his own situation. He was very old now, well past the age of having children. His wife was also elderly and had always been barren - unable to have babies.

Zakariya and his wife had never had children, and now they were both so old that having a baby seemed completely impossible by all natural laws.

But watching Maryam receive miraculous food made Zakariya realize something important: Allah is not limited by what seems possible or impossible! If Allah can send food from nowhere, He can certainly give children to elderly people!

The Quran tells us: "At that, Zakariya called upon his Lord..."

Inspired by Maryam's miracles and her simple, powerful faith, Zakariya decided to ask Allah for something that seemed impossible. If Allah provides for Maryam "without measure," surely He could provide Zakariya with something he deeply desired - a child to continue his legacy of faith and prophethood!

Right there, near Maryam's chamber, Zakariya raised his hands and made a beautiful, private prayer to Allah - a prayer that would also be answered miraculously!

inspire.title: The Day the Angels Came
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 4 

Maryam continued her life of worship and devotion in the temple. She was now a young woman - pure, modest, and completely dedicated to Allah. She had no interest in the worldly life. She spent her days and nights in prayer, fasting, and reading the scriptures.

One day, as Maryam was praying in her private chamber, something extraordinary happened. Angels appeared before her!

She couldn't see them with her eyes, but she could hear their voices clearly. They spoke to her with the most beautiful words:

"O Maryam! Indeed, Allah has chosen you and purified you. He has chosen you above all women of the worlds!"

Can you imagine? Allah's angels, carrying a message from Allah Himself, telling Maryam that she was chosen above ALL women who had ever lived or would ever live!

The angels continued: "O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord. Prostrate and bow with those who bow in prayer."

This was encouragement to keep doing what she was already doing - worshipping Allah with dedication and humility.

But Maryam didn't let this praise make her proud. She didn't think, "I'm so special!" or "I'm better than everyone!" No! She remained humble and continued her worship exactly as before, perhaps even more earnestly.

Then, some time later, the angels came again with a message that would change Maryam's life forever. This time, their news was shocking and confusing:

"O Maryam! Indeed, Allah gives you good news of a word from Him! His name will be the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam!"

The angels continued describing this child: He will be distinguished in this world and in the Hereafter, he will be among those close to Allah, he will speak to people while still in the cradle and as an adult, and he will be among the righteous.

Maryam was confused and startled. A son? A baby? But how could this be?

"My Lord," she said, trembling, "how can I have a child when no man has touched me?"

You see, Maryam was not married. She had never been with a man. She had lived her entire life in purity and chastity, dedicated only to worshipping Allah. The very idea of having a baby seemed impossible - and more than that, it seemed like it would ruin her reputation!

What would people say? How would she explain this? Everyone knew she had been living in the temple, devoted to worship. If she suddenly had a baby without being married, people would think terrible things about her! They would accuse her of shameful behavior!

But the angels explained: "He said: 'Such is Allah. He creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.'"

In other words: Allah doesn't need normal means to do things! He created Adam without a father OR a mother - just from clay! He created Hawwa (Eve) from Adam without a mother! And now, He would create Isa from a mother without a father!

It was a miracle, a sign for all humanity that Allah can do anything! When Allah wants something to happen, He simply says "Be!" and it happens instantly!

The angels continued, telling Maryam more about this miraculous child: Allah would teach him the Scripture, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel (Injeel). He would be a messenger to the Children of Israel. He would perform many miracles by Allah's permission. He would call people to worship Allah alone.

Maryam listened to all of this in awe and wonder. She was chosen for something no other woman had ever been chosen for - to give birth to a prophet without a father, through a miracle from Allah!

She was equal to other women

inspire.title: The Miraculous Conception
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 5 

After the angels gave Maryam the news, she was left alone with her thoughts. How would this happen? When would it happen? What should she do?

Maryam continued her worship and devoted life as always, but now with this knowledge that something miraculous was going to happen to her.

One day, Maryam needed to leave her chamber in the temple. The Quran mentions that she "withdrew from her family to a place in the east" - meaning she went to a private, secluded place, perhaps to pray or to fulfill a need.

She wanted complete privacy, so she put up a screen or curtain to separate herself from people's view. This showed her modesty and her constant care for her reputation and honor.

While she was alone behind this screen, suddenly someone appeared before her! It was the figure of a man - perfectly formed, handsome, and glowing with light!

Maryam was terrified! Who was this man? How did he get here? What did he want?

She immediately sought Allah's protection and said: "I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you! If you fear Allah, don't come near me!"

What a beautiful response! Even in her fear, her first instinct was to call on Allah and remind this stranger to fear Allah!

But this was no ordinary man. This was the angel Jibreel (Gabriel), who had taken on human form so he could speak with Maryam!

Jibreel said gently: "I am only a messenger from your Lord, sent to give you the gift of a pure son."

But Maryam was still confused and worried. She said: "How can I have a son when no man has touched me, and I have not been unchaste?"

She was essentially saying: "I am pure! I have never done anything wrong! How can I have a baby?"

Jibreel replied with the same message the angels had given her before: "Thus said your Lord: 'It is easy for Me. We will make him a sign for humanity and a mercy from Us. It is a matter already decided.'"

Then, the Quran tells us: "So he breathed into her."

Jibreel, by Allah's command, blew toward Maryam (some scholars say he blew into the sleeve of her garment). Through this breath, by Allah's will and power, Maryam conceived a child!

There was no physical relationship, no father in the biological sense. This was a pure miracle - the creation of a human life through Allah's direct command, carried out through the breath of the angel!

At that moment, Maryam became pregnant with Prophet Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him!

Imagine how Maryam must have felt! She knew this was Allah's will. She believed the angels' message. But she also knew what was coming - the shock of her people, the accusations, the shame she would face when everyone saw her pregnant without being married!

Still, Maryam submitted to Allah's decree. She didn't run away or try to hide forever. She accepted that this was her test, her trial, and her honor all at once!

The pregnancy progressed naturally. Maryam felt the baby growing inside her, just like any expectant mother would. But unlike other expectant mothers, Maryam carried her secret alone, knowing that a time would come when she would have to face the world with this miraculous but unexplainable situation!

options: She sought refuge in Allah and told him to fear Allah

options: The angel Jibreel in human form

inspire.title: The Pain of Loneliness
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 6 

As Maryam's pregnancy progressed, she faced a difficult situation. She was carrying a baby, but she had no husband. How could she explain this to people?

Even though the angels had told her this was Allah's will, even though she knew she had done nothing wrong, Maryam knew that people would not understand. They would accuse her of terrible things. They would say she had been unchaste. They would mock her and shame her family!

The stress and worry must have been overwhelming for this young woman who had spent her whole life in purity and worship!

As her pregnancy advanced and became more visible, Maryam made a decision. She could not stay in Jerusalem where everyone knew her. She had to go somewhere else to give birth in privacy.

So Maryam left the temple and the city. She traveled alone, pregnant and vulnerable, into the wilderness. Can you imagine how difficult this must have been? A young woman, alone, pregnant, walking through the desert with no one to help her!

The Quran tells us: "So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a distant place."

She walked and walked until she reached a remote area - far from the city, far from people, far from judgment and accusing eyes.

But being alone also meant being without help. When the time came for her to give birth, there was no midwife, no mother or aunt to comfort her, no female relatives to help. She was completely alone!

The pains of childbirth began. Maryam felt the contractions, the pain, the fear of giving birth with no one to help her. She was exhausted from the journey, scared about the birth, and overwhelmed by what would come after!

She found herself near a dried-up palm tree. The labor pains became stronger and stronger. She leaned against the trunk of the palm tree, gripping it for support as waves of pain washed over her.

In that moment of intense physical pain and emotional anguish, Maryam cried out words that show just how human and vulnerable she was:

"Oh, I wish I had died before this and had been forgotten completely!"

It was a cry of despair! She wasn't really wishing for death - she was simply overwhelmed! The pain, the loneliness, the fear of what people would say, the worry about how she would raise this child - it all came crashing down on her in that moment!

Think about it: This was the woman Allah had chosen above all other women. The woman the angels had praised. The woman who had received miraculous food from heaven. But right now, she was alone, in pain, scared, and overwhelmed!

This teaches us something beautiful: Even the most righteous people face moments of weakness, pain, and difficulty! Even those closest to Allah have times when they feel overwhelmed and wish for relief!

Maryam's words were not a complaint against Allah - they were an honest expression of human emotion in an incredibly difficult moment. And Allah understood. He didn't punish her for this moment of weakness. Instead, He was about to send her comfort and help!

inspire.title: The Comfort from Allah
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 7 

Just when Maryam felt she couldn't bear anymore, when she had cried out in despair, Allah sent her comfort in the most beautiful way!

As Maryam leaned against the palm tree, in the peak of her pain and loneliness, she heard a voice! The Quran tells us that either the angel Jibreel or the baby Isa himself called out to her from below:

"Don't be sad! Your Lord has provided a stream beneath you!"

Maryam looked down, and there it was - fresh, clean, flowing water! In the middle of the dry desert, Allah had created a stream just for her! She could drink and refresh herself!

Then the voice said: "And shake the trunk of the palm tree toward you. It will drop fresh, ripe dates upon you!"

Maryam looked up at the palm tree she was leaning against. It was dried up, dead-looking, with no fruit on it. But Allah commanded her to shake it!

Even in her weakness and pain, Maryam obeyed. She shook the tree trunk. Immediately, fresh, delicious, ripe dates began to fall down around her! The dead tree came alive and gave fruit!

These weren't just any dates - they were the best kind for a woman who had just given birth! Dates give energy, help with healing, and increase milk production. Allah knew exactly what Maryam needed and provided it miraculously!

Then the voice gave her one more instruction: "So eat and drink and be content. And if you see any human, say: 'I have vowed silence to the Most Merciful, so I will not speak today to any person.'"

What a wise command! Allah was telling Maryam: "Don't try to explain or defend yourself with words. Let Me handle this. Just stay silent and trust Me."

So Maryam had fresh water to drink, nutritious dates to eat, and instructions to remain silent. Allah had taken care of her physical needs and given her a strategy for dealing with people's questions!

And then, in that remote place, supported by miracles from Allah, Maryam gave birth to a baby boy - Prophet Isa, peace be upon him!

The baby was born healthy and perfect. Maryam held him in her arms, this miraculous child who had no earthly father. She felt a mixture of emotions - love for her baby, relief that the birth was over, but also worry about what would come next.

She stayed there for some time - some scholars say 40 days - recovering from childbirth, taking care of her baby, drinking from the stream, eating the dates, and gathering her strength.

Allah had not abandoned her in her most difficult moment. When she felt weakest and most alone, He had provided for her in miraculous ways! The stream, the dates, and the healthy baby were all signs of Allah's care and mercy.

But now, she had to face the hardest part - returning to her people with a baby and no husband!

inspire.title: Facing the People
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 8 

After recovering from childbirth and gathering her strength, Maryam knew she couldn't hide forever. She had to return to her people. She had to face them with this baby.

With great courage, Maryam wrapped baby Isa warmly and began the journey back to Jerusalem. Every step closer to the city probably filled her with anxiety. What would people say? How would they react?

When she entered the city carrying a baby, people immediately recognized her. "That's Maryam! The girl from the temple! The one dedicated to worship!" They looked at the baby in her arms with shock and disbelief.

Word spread quickly through the town. People came out of their houses. They gathered around her. Their faces showed shock, disappointment, and anger.

The Children of Israel - her own people - began to confront her harshly:

"O Maryam! You have done something terrible!"
"O sister of Harun (Aaron)! Your father was not an evil man, and your mother was not unchaste! How could you do this?"

They were calling her "sister of Harun," referring to Harun the brother of Prophet Musa - meaning "you come from a righteous family! How could you bring such shame?"

They were accusing her of the worst sin - having a relationship with a man outside of marriage! They thought she had destroyed her reputation and her family's honor!

The crowd grew larger and more hostile. People were shouting accusations. Some were mocking her. Others were shaking their heads in disappointment. The woman who had been respected and admired for her devotion was now being shamed publicly!

Maryam must have felt her heart breaking. These were her people! She had grown up among them! And now they were treating her like she was the worst person in the world!

But Maryam remembered what she had been commanded to do. She didn't try to explain. She didn't try to defend herself with words. She simply pointed to the baby in her arms!

The people looked at her in confusion. "What? You want us to talk to a baby? How can we speak to an infant in the cradle? Are you mocking us now?"

They thought Maryam had gone crazy! First she brings a baby with no husband, and now she wants them to talk to the baby? This made them even more angry!

But then something absolutely miraculous happened - something that would silence all the accusers and prove Maryam's innocence beyond any doubt!

The baby Isa, just a newborn infant, opened his mouth and spoke! Not baby sounds or crying - clear, eloquent speech!

In a strong, clear voice, baby Isa declared:

"Indeed, I am the servant of Allah! He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet!"

The crowd fell silent. Everyone froze. Did that baby just... speak?!

The tiny infant continued:

"And He has made me blessed wherever I am. He has commanded me to pray and give charity as long as I live, and to be dutiful to my mother. He has not made me arrogant or miserable. Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive!"

The baby - probably just 40 days old - had just delivered a sermon! He had declared his prophethood, explained his mission, honored his mother, and described his entire life from birth to death to resurrection!

The people stood in absolute shock. Some fell to their knees. Others covered their mouths in amazement. Their accusations died on their lips!

This was clearly a miracle from Allah! No ordinary baby could speak like this! This was a sign that Maryam was innocent, that this baby was special, and that Allah had a great purpose for him!

Maryam's reputation was saved! Allah had defended her in a way no words of hers could have done!

inspire.title: The Childhood of Isa - Growing in Wisdom and Miracles
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 9 

After the miraculous speech from baby Isa, the people of Jerusalem could no longer deny that something special had happened. Some believed that Isa was indeed a prophet from Allah. Others remained skeptical but couldn't deny what they had witnessed.

Maryam raised Isa with great care and devotion. She taught him to worship Allah, to be kind and gentle, and to serve others. Even as a child, Isa was different from other children!

While other boys played games and got into trouble, young Isa was serious, thoughtful, and wise beyond his years. He loved to worship Allah, to help people, and to learn about the scriptures.

Allah gave Isa knowledge and wisdom even as a child. The Quran tells us: "And He will teach him the Scripture and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel."

Isa learned the Torah - the book that had been revealed to Prophet Musa - and understood it deeply. He didn't just memorize words; he understood the meanings, the wisdom, and the purpose behind each teaching!

As Isa grew older, people began to notice his remarkable character: He was incredibly kind and compassionate, he never lied, not even small lies, he helped the poor and the sick, he spoke with wisdom that impressed even the learned scholars, he was patient when people were rude to him, and he was humble despite his knowledge and abilities.

But what made Isa truly unique were the miracles that Allah allowed him to perform - miracles that showed he was no ordinary child!

Allah had given Isa special abilities as signs of his prophethood. These weren't magic tricks - they were real miracles done by Allah's permission to prove that Isa was His messenger!

Some of the miracles young Isa performed included:

Creating birds from clay: Isa would take clay and shape it into the form of a bird. Then, by Allah's permission, he would breathe into it, and it would become a real, living bird that would fly away! This showed that Allah, who created all life, had given Isa power over creation!

Healing the sick: People who had been sick for years would come to Isa. He would place his hands on them or pray for them, and by Allah's permission, they would be healed instantly! Blind people could suddenly see! Deaf people could hear! Those with leprosy (a terrible skin disease) were cured!

Knowing hidden things: Isa could tell people what they had eaten in their homes and what they had stored away! He had knowledge of unseen things that only Allah could have given him!

These miracles amazed the people, but Isa was always careful to make one thing clear: "I do these things by Allah's permission, not by my own power! I am Allah's servant and messenger!"

He never claimed to be doing these miracles on his own. He never claimed to be divine. He always pointed people back to Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of everything!

As Isa grew from a child into a young man, his reputation spread throughout the land. People would come from far and wide to see him, to learn from him, and to witness his miracles.

But not everyone was happy about Isa's growing influence. The religious leaders of the Children of Israel - the priests, scribes, and Pharisees - began to watch him carefully. They were jealous of his popularity and worried that he might threaten their authority!

Still, Isa continued his mission: calling people to worship Allah alone, teaching them to be kind and just, and showing them through his miracles that Allah is All-Powerful!

inspire.title: The Message of Isa - Returning to the Pure Faith
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 10 

When Isa reached about thirty years old, Allah sent him as a prophet to the Children of Israel with a clear message!

The Children of Israel had gone astray in many ways. They had the Torah from Prophet Musa, but over the centuries, they had added their own rules and changed some of Allah's teachings. They had made religion complicated and burdensome!

Some of their problems: They focused on following detailed rules but ignored justice and mercy, they changed parts of the scripture to suit their desires, the religious leaders loved their positions and wealth more than truth, they looked down on the poor and sinners instead of helping them, and they forgot that the most important thing is loving Allah and being kind to people.

So Allah sent Isa to bring them back to the pure, simple message: Worship Allah alone and treat people with kindness!

Isa announced: "Indeed, I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming the Torah that came before me!"

He honored the Torah and the prophets who came before him. He didn't claim to bring a completely new religion - he was continuing the same message that all prophets brought: worship Allah alone!

But Isa also brought something new: the Injeel (Gospel) - a new scripture from Allah that provided guidance and mercy!

Isa's message was beautiful and simple:

Love Allah above everything: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your mind!"

Be kind to everyone: Treat others the way you want to be treated. Help the poor. Visit the sick. Be humble. Forgive those who hurt you!

Don't be hypocrites: The religious leaders would pray publicly to show off, but their hearts were not sincere. Isa told people: "When you pray, don't be like the hypocrites! Pray sincerely, even in private!"

True faith is internal, not just external: It's not enough to follow rules outwardly. Your heart must be pure! It's better to have a clean heart and make mistakes than to look perfect but have a corrupt heart!

Isa also told them good news: "And I bring you good news of a messenger who will come after me. His name will be Ahmad (Muhammad)."

Yes! Isa told the Children of Israel about the final prophet who would come - Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) - who would complete the message to all of humanity!

Isa gathered disciples (Al-Hawariyun) - a group of sincere believers who followed him and helped spread his message. They were simple men - fishermen and workers - but they had pure hearts!

These disciples traveled with Isa, learned from him, witnessed his miracles, and helped teach people about Allah!

One famous story about the disciples shows their faith and also their human weakness:

One day, the disciples said to Isa: "Can your Lord send down to us a table of food from heaven?"

Isa was surprised. "Fear Allah if you are truly believers! Why do you need this when you've seen so many miracles already?"

They replied: "We want to eat from it, so our hearts will be content, and we will know you have told us the truth, and we can be witnesses to it!"

So Isa prayed: "O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven to be a festival for us - for the first of us and the last of us - and a sign from You! And provide for us, for You are the best of providers!"

Allah answered: "Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that, I will punish them with a punishment I have never inflicted on anyone in the worlds!"

And Allah sent down a table of food from heaven! It was a miracle and a test. This feast became a festival, and it was proof of Allah's power!

options: They complicated religion and ignored justice and mercy

options: Worship Allah alone and treat people with kindness

inspire.title: The Growing Opposition - When Truth Threatens Power
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 12 

As Isa's message spread and more people followed him, the religious leaders of the Children of Israel became increasingly worried and angry!

These leaders - the chief priests, scribes, and Pharisees - had power, wealth, and respect. They didn't want anyone challenging their authority! And Isa was definitely challenging them!

Isa criticized them publicly for their hypocrisy. He said things like:

"Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You look righteous outwardly, but inside you are full of greed and self-indulgence!"

"You travel over land and sea to make one convert, and when you succeed, you make them twice as much a child of hell as yourselves!"

"You've abandoned the important matters of the law - justice, mercy, and faithfulness - for minor details!"

These were harsh words! But they were true! The religious leaders were more interested in their positions and wealth than in truly serving Allah and helping people!

The leaders were furious! Who was this young man to criticize them? They had spent years studying the scriptures! They held important positions! How dare he speak to them this way!

They started plotting against Isa:

"He's dangerous! He's turning the people against us!"
"He performs miracles, and people are starting to believe in him more than they believe in us!"
"If we let him continue, soon no one will listen to us anymore!"
"He claims to be a prophet, but he goes against some of our traditions!"

But what really bothered them wasn't theology or religious differences. It was power! They were afraid of losing control over the people!

They tried to trap Isa with difficult questions, hoping he would say something they could use against him. But Isa's wisdom was too great! He answered every question perfectly!

They tried to catch him breaking their religious laws, but Isa was righteous in everything he did!

They sent spies to follow him, hoping to find some fault or scandal. But Isa's life was pure and blameless!

The more they tried to discredit him, the more people believed in him! His miracles were undeniable. His message was pure. His character was perfect. Even some of the religious leaders secretly believed in him but were too afraid to say so publicly!

Finally, the leaders decided they had to get rid of Isa completely. They began to plot how they could arrest him and have him executed!

But they had a problem: Isa was very popular with the common people! If they arrested him openly, the people might riot! So they needed to be sneaky about it.

They decided to use one of Isa's own followers to betray him!

Among Isa's disciples was a man who was not sincere. He appeared to be a follower, but his heart was not truly with Isa. The leaders approached this disciple and offered him money - thirty pieces of silver - to help them capture Isa!

The greedy disciple agreed! He would betray his teacher for money!

The religious leaders were pleased with their evil plan. They thought: "Soon, this troublemaker will be gone, and things will go back to the way they were. We will have our power and respect back!"

But they didn't know that Allah had a completely different plan - a plan that would shock everyone and prove once and for all that Allah protects His prophets!

inspire.title: The Great Miracle - Allah's Protection of Isa
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 13 

The religious leaders had made their plan. They had their betrayer ready. They gathered soldiers and weapons. They went to arrest Isa at night, thinking they would capture him easily and execute him!

But Allah knew about their plot. And Allah had a different plan entirely - one that would prove His power and protect His prophet!

The Quran tells us what really happened: "And for their saying, 'Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of Allah.' But they killed him not, nor crucified him. Rather, it was made to appear so to them!"

What does this mean? What really happened that night?

When the soldiers came to arrest Isa, Allah saved him in a miraculous way!

According to Islamic teachings, Allah raised Isa up to the heavens - body and soul - alive! Isa did not die! He was not crucified! He was lifted up by Allah's power to a place of safety!

But Allah made someone else look exactly like Isa - either the betrayer himself or one of the soldiers. This person who looked like Isa was arrested, beaten, and crucified instead!

The people thought they were crucifying Isa, but they were wrong! They were crucifying someone who looked like him!

The Quran says: "And those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain!"

So what happened was: The enemies came to arrest Isa, Allah raised Isa to the heavens, alive and well, Allah made someone else look exactly like Isa, that person was arrested and crucified, and the people thought they had killed Isa, but they were confused and uncertain.

Even the disciples were confused! Some saw Isa being arrested, and later heard he was crucified. But how could their beloved teacher, who performed such miracles, be killed? Some of them were uncertain about what really happened!

The Quran makes it absolutely clear: "Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise."

Isa was not killed! He is alive with Allah in the heavens! His body was not crucified! He did not die on the cross!

This is one of the key differences between Islamic belief and Christian belief. Christians believe Jesus was crucified and died for people's sins. Muslims believe that Allah saved Isa from crucifixion, that he did not die, and that Allah raised him to the heavens alive!

Why is this important? Because:

It shows Allah's power: Allah can save His prophets however He wants! No group of people can defeat Allah's plan!

It shows Allah's justice: Allah does not let His innocent prophets be humiliated and killed by evil people! He honors and protects them!

It clarifies Isa's role: Isa was a prophet and messenger, not a divine being or sacrifice for sins! Allah does not need anyone to die for people's sins. If you repent sincerely, Allah forgives you directly!

The Quran says: "It is not befitting for Allah to take a son! Exalted is He! When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is!"

Isa himself never claimed to be God or the son of God. He was Allah's servant and messenger, just like all the prophets before him!

inspire.title: What Isa Really Taught - The True Message
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 14 

Now that we know the story of Prophet Isa's life and how Allah saved him, let's talk about what Isa really taught, because many people today have misunderstood his message!

Isa's message was clear and simple, just like the message of all prophets before and after him:

1. Worship Allah Alone - No Partners!

Isa never said, "Worship me!" He never claimed to be God! He never said he was the son of God in a literal sense!

When someone called him "Good Teacher," Isa responded: "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone!"

Isa prayed to Allah, which means he worshipped Allah! If Isa were God, who was he praying to? You can't pray to yourself!

The Quran tells us that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will ask Isa: "O Isa, son of Maryam, did you tell the people to take you and your mother as gods besides Allah?"

And Isa will reply: "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say what I had no right to say! If I had said it, You would have known it! You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself! Indeed, it is You who knows all the unseen! I only said to them what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord!'"

This is the truth! Isa taught people to worship Allah, not himself!

2. Isa Was Human, Not Divine

Isa ate food, drank water, slept, and felt pain - all signs that he was human, not divine!

Allah says in the Quran: "The Messiah, son of Maryam, was not but a messenger. Other messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food!"

Why does Allah mention that they ate food? Because gods don't need food! Eating is a sign of need and weakness. Someone who needs food and drink is dependent on something else - they cannot be God!

3. The Trinity Was Never Isa's Teaching

The concept of the Trinity (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit) was invented by people after Isa was raised to the heavens!

Isa himself never taught this! He taught simple, pure monotheism - worship Allah alone!

The Quran says: "They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'Allah is the third of three.' But there is no god except one God!"

4. No One Dies for Another's Sins

In Islam, we believe that everyone is responsible for their own actions! No one can carry another person's sins!

The Quran says: "And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another!"

You cannot send someone else to be punished for your mistakes! If you sin, you must repent to Allah yourself! And if you repent sincerely, Allah will forgive you directly - no sacrifice or intermediary needed!

Allah is the Most Merciful! He forgives all sins if you turn to Him with sincere repentance!

5. Isa Will Return!

Here's something amazing: Muslims believe that Isa is still alive with Allah in the heavens, and he will return to Earth before the Day of Judgment!

When he returns, he will: Descend from the heavens to Earth, correct the false beliefs about him, tell Christians: "I never asked you to worship me! I only told you to worship Allah!", break the cross (showing it's not a symbol of salvation), live among people and rule with justice, and die a natural death (because all humans must taste death eventually).

His return will be one of the major signs that the Day of Judgment is near!

6. What Should We Believe About Isa?

As Muslims, we love and respect Prophet Isa deeply! We believe: He was a great prophet and messenger of Allah, he was born miraculously without a father, he performed amazing miracles by Allah's permission, he brought the Injeel (Gospel) as guidance, he was not killed or crucified, but raised to the heavens, he will return before the Day of Judgment, and he was a servant of Allah, not God or the son of God.

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever believes in me and disbelieves in Isa is not a believer. And whoever believes in Isa and disbelieves in me is not a believer."

This means Muslims must believe in both prophets!

inspire.title: Maryam and Isa - A Final Reflection
inspire.content:
## Prophet Isa ibn Maryam (AS) Part - 15 

Let's end our stories about Prophet Isa by reflecting on what his story, and his mother Maryam's story, teach us today.

The Story of Maryam Teaches Us:

Faith in impossible situations: When Maryam was told she would have a baby without a husband, it seemed impossible and terrifying. But she trusted Allah's plan, even though she didn't understand it fully!

Patience with people's judgment: Maryam faced terrible accusations from her own people. They thought the worst of her! But she remained patient and let Allah defend her. And He did - in the most miraculous way!

Allah's support for the righteous: When Maryam was alone in the desert, in pain, scared, and helpless, Allah sent her water, food, and comfort. Allah never abandons those who are sincere!

The power of dedication to worship: Maryam spent her youth in devotion to Allah, and Allah honored her above all women. When you dedicate yourself to Allah, He elevates you in ways you cannot imagine!

Modesty and purity: Maryam guarded her chastity and modesty carefully. She is held up in the Quran as the perfect example of a pure, righteous woman!

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "The best women of Paradise are Maryam, Fatimah (his daughter), Asiya (wife of Fir'awn), and Khadijah (his wife)."

Maryam is honored so much that an entire chapter of the Quran (Surah 19) is named after her! She is the only woman mentioned by name in the entire Quran!

The Story of Isa Teaches Us:

Miracles don't make you God: Isa performed amazing miracles - healing the sick, giving sight to the blind, even creating birds from clay! But he always made it clear: "I do this by Allah's permission!" Having special abilities doesn't make you divine!

Humility despite greatness: Isa was a great prophet with incredible knowledge and power, but he remained humble. He served the poor, washed people's feet, and treated everyone with kindness!

Speaking truth to power: Isa wasn't afraid to criticize the corrupt religious leaders, even though they had power and could harm him. When you see injustice, speak up - even if it costs you!

Allah protects His messengers: When enemies plotted to kill Isa, Allah saved him in a miraculous way. This teaches us that no one can defeat Allah's plan!

The same message throughout history: Isa confirmed the prophets before him and told people about the prophet who would come after him (Muhammad). This shows that all prophets brought the same basic message!

For Children Today:

If you're a young person reading these stories, here's what you can learn:

Be dedicated to Allah from a young age: You don't have to wait until you're grown up to be close to Allah! Maryam was devoted to worship even as a young girl!

Don't let people's opinions stop you from doing right: Maryam faced terrible accusations, but she knew she was innocent. Do what's right, even if people misunderstand you!

Trust Allah in difficult times: When Maryam cried out in pain and despair, Allah immediately sent help. Turn to Allah in your difficulties!

Use your abilities to help others: If Allah gives you talents - whether you're smart, athletic, artistic, or anything else - use those gifts to help people, like Isa used his miracles!

Stand firm in your beliefs: Don't let anyone pressure you into believing something false about Allah or His prophets. Know the truth and hold onto it!

The Story Continues:

Prophet Isa's story hasn't ended! He is alive with Allah in the heavens, and he will return to Earth before the Day of Judgment!

When he returns, he will clarify the truth about himself. He will tell people: "I never claimed to be God! I only called you to worship Allah alone!"

And all of us - Muslims, Christians, Jews, and everyone - will stand before Allah on the Day of Judgment and answer for what we believed and how we lived!

On that Day, Isa will be there as a witness. Maryam will be there, honored and pure. And the truth will be clear to everyone!

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the son of Maryam will soon descend among you as a just ruler!"

Final Reminder: When you hear about "Jesus Christ" in school or see Christmas decorations or hear Christian beliefs, remember the true story of Prophet Isa! He was a blessed messenger who called people to worship Allah alone. He never claimed divinity, and Allah saved him from crucifixion!

Love and respect him as Muslims do - as one of the greatest prophets, but still a human being and servant of Allah!

And when someone asks you, "Do you believe in Jesus?" you can say with confidence: "Yes! I believe in Prophet Isa, peace be upon him. I believe he was a great messenger of Allah, born miraculously to Maryam, performed amazing miracles, and will return before the Day of Judgment. But I don't believe he was God or the son of God, because he himself taught us to worship only Allah!"

inspire.title: The Truthful Friend
inspire.content:
Abu Bakr was Prophet Muhammad's best friend. They were so close that people called Abu Bakr 'As-Siddiq' which means 'The Truthful One.'

One night, something amazing happened. The Prophet told everyone that he had traveled from Makkah to Jerusalem and then to the heavens, all in one night! This journey is called Al-Isra wal Mi'raj.

Many people didn't believe it. They laughed and said, "That's impossible! How can someone travel so far in one night?"

But when they asked Abu Bakr, "Do you believe your friend?", he didn't hesitate for even a second. He said, "If Muhammad said it, then I believe him. I believe him in things even more amazing than this!"

Abu Bakr believed in his friend completely because he knew the Prophet never lied. He didn't need to see it with his own eyes to know it was true.

The Prophet was so happy with Abu Bakr's faith that he smiled and said Abu Bakr truly deserved the name 'As-Siddiq - The Truthful One.'

## Lesson Learned: 

True friends believe in each other and stand by each other, especially when times are tough. Trust and loyalty are the foundations of real friendship.

inspire.title: The Man Who Gave Everything
inspire.content:
Abu Bakr was a wealthy merchant in Makkah, but he used his wealth in the most beautiful way - to help others.

When Muslims were being hurt and treated badly in Makkah, Abu Bakr would use his money to buy slaves who had accepted Islam and set them free. One of them was Bilal, who would later become the first caller to prayer in Islam.

One day, the Prophet asked all the Muslims to bring whatever they could to help prepare for a battle. People brought different amounts - some brought a little, some brought more.

When Abu Bakr arrived, the Prophet asked him, "What did you leave for your family?"

Abu Bakr smiled and said, "I left them Allah and His Messenger."

He had brought everything he owned! His entire wealth! The Prophet's eyes filled with tears of joy at seeing such generosity.

Umar, another great companion, said later, "I can never beat Abu Bakr in doing good deeds. Whatever I do, he has already done more!"

## Lesson Learned: 

True generosity means giving even when it's hard. When you help others and trust in Allah, He will always take care of you and your family.

inspire.title: The Brave Leader Who Changed
inspire.content:
Before Umar became Muslim, he was one of the strongest and scariest men in Makkah. He was so angry at Muslims that one day he decided to go and hurt the Prophet.

On his way, someone told him, "Umar, before you go to Muhammad, you should know that your own sister and her husband have become Muslims!"

Umar was shocked! He went straight to his sister's house. When he arrived, he heard her reading the Quran. He got very angry and pushed his sister. But when he saw her bleeding, his heart softened.

His sister was brave. She said, "Yes, Umar, we are Muslims. Do what you want, but we will not leave our faith!"

Umar felt ashamed. He asked to read what they were reciting. It was Surah Ta-Ha from the Quran. As he read the beautiful words, tears rolled down his strong face.

Right away, Umar went to the Prophet and said, "I want to become Muslim!"

The Prophet and all the Muslims were so happy! The Prophet had prayed for Umar to accept Islam, and Allah answered his prayer. From that day, Umar became one of Islam's greatest defenders.

## Lesson Learned: 

It's never too late to change and become better. Even the strongest and toughest people can have soft hearts. Everyone deserves a second chance.

inspire.title: The Leader Who Checked on His People at Night
inspire.content:
When Umar became the leader of the Muslims, he ruled over a huge area. But even though he was so powerful, he never forgot about the ordinary people.

Every night, Umar would disguise himself in simple clothes and walk through the streets of Madinah to see if anyone needed help.

One night, he heard a baby crying in a tent. He went closer and saw a mother trying to calm her hungry children. She had a pot on the fire, but there was only water and stones in it!

Umar asked, "Why are you boiling stones?"

The mother said sadly, "My children are hungry, but I have no food. I'm pretending to cook so they will fall asleep thinking food is coming."

Umar's heart broke. He ran back to the treasury, filled a large bag with flour, dates, and oil, and carried it on his own back to the woman's tent.

His servant offered to carry it, but Umar said, "Will you carry my burden on the Day of Judgment too?"

He cooked the food himself until the children ate and smiled. Only then did Umar leave, making sure no one in his city would go hungry again.

## Lesson Learned: 

Good leaders care about everyone, especially those who are struggling. When you have the power to help, you should use it to make others happy.

inspire.title: The Shy Man Who Gave Water to a City
inspire.content:
Uthman was known for being very shy and very rich. He was so shy that even the angels felt shy around him! But when it came to helping people, Uthman was always first.

When the Muslims came to Madinah, they faced a big problem. There was only one well with good water, and it belonged to a man who charged a lot of money for it. Poor Muslims couldn't afford to drink!

The Prophet said, "Who will buy this well and make it free for all Muslims? Allah will give them a garden in Paradise."

Uthman immediately went to the owner and asked, "Will you sell me your well?"

The man said, "It costs a very high price - 20,000 dirhams!"

Without hesitation, Uthman said, "I'll buy it!" He paid the huge amount and made the well free for everyone.

From that day on, any Muslim could drink from the well without paying anything. The poor, the rich, travelers, and even animals - all could drink freely.

Years later, people were still drinking from that well, and Uthman was still earning rewards in his grave for every single drop of water they drank.

## Lesson Learned: 

When you help others, the rewards keep coming even after you're gone. Spending money on helping people is the best investment you can ever make.

inspire.title: The Man Who Equipped an Entire Army
inspire.content:
The Muslims were preparing to face their enemies in a battle called Tabuk. But there was a big problem - they didn't have enough supplies! No horses, no camels, no weapons, and no food for such a long journey.

The Prophet called out, "Who will help prepare this army? Allah will reward them greatly!"

Uthman stood up and said, "I will provide 100 camels with all their supplies!"

Everyone was amazed! But Uthman wasn't done. He said, "I will add another 100 camels!"

The Prophet was so happy that he raised his hands and prayed, "O Allah, be pleased with Uthman, for I am pleased with him!"

But Uthman still wasn't finished! He kept giving and giving until he had equipped almost one-third of the entire army! He provided camels, horses, food, water, weapons - everything the soldiers needed.

The Prophet was so moved that he said, "Nothing Uthman does after today will harm him!" This meant that Uthman had earned such great rewards that Allah would always be pleased with him.

## Lesson Learned: 

When people are in need, give as much as you can. Don't just give a little and stop - if you can do more, do it! Allah loves those who give generously.

inspire.title: The Boy Who Slept in Danger's Bed
inspire.content:
Ali was the Prophet's young cousin, and he loved the Prophet more than anything in the world.

One night, the enemies of Islam made an evil plan. They decided to attack the Prophet's house at night and hurt him while he slept. They surrounded his house, waiting for the perfect moment.

But Allah told the Prophet about their plan. The Prophet needed to leave Makkah secretly that night to go to Madinah. But who would sleep in his bed so the enemies would think he was still there?

The Prophet asked young Ali, "Will you sleep in my bed tonight? The enemies are outside, and it will be very dangerous."

Ali didn't hesitate even for a second. He said, "Yes! Will you be safe if I do this?"

The Prophet said, "Yes."

Ali smiled and said, "Then I will do it happily!"

That night, while the enemies waited outside with their swords, Ali calmly lay down in the Prophet's bed, covered himself with the Prophet's green blanket, and went to sleep! He wasn't afraid at all because he knew he was protecting someone he loved.

When the enemies burst in at dawn, they were shocked to find Ali instead of the Prophet. The Prophet was already safely on his way to Madinah.

## Lesson Learned: 

True bravery means protecting others even when you're afraid. When you love someone, you're willing to sacrifice for them.

inspire.title: The Gate to the City of Knowledge
inspire.content:
Ali grew up in the Prophet's house, learning directly from him every single day. He watched everything the Prophet did and listened carefully to everything he said.

The Prophet loved Ali's eagerness to learn. One day, he told everyone, "I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate."

This meant that if you wanted to reach the Prophet's knowledge, you should learn from Ali!

Ali had an amazing memory. He remembered everything the Prophet taught him. But he didn't just memorize - he understood deeply and thought carefully about everything.

When people came to Ali with difficult questions, he would think carefully before answering. He would say, "Let me think about what the Prophet taught us about this."

Ali was also known for his wise sayings. He would say things like: "Knowledge is better than wealth. Knowledge guards you, while you have to guard wealth!" and "Your enemy is not the one who is far from you, but the one who is inside you - your bad habits!"

Even though Ali was young, people traveled from far away to learn from him because of his deep understanding and wisdom.

## Lesson Learned: 

Learning is not just about memorizing facts - it's about understanding deeply and thinking carefully. True knowledge helps you become wise and helps others too.

inspire.title: The Man Who Became a Shield
inspire.content:
Talha was a brave companion who loved the Prophet so much that he was willing to give his life to protect him.

During the Battle of Uhud, the Muslims were winning at first. But then something went wrong, and suddenly the Prophet was in great danger! Enemies surrounded him from all sides, shooting arrows and swinging swords.

When Talha saw this, he ran as fast as he could toward the Prophet. He didn't think about himself at all - he only wanted to save the Prophet!

Talha used his own body as a shield! He stood in front of the Prophet and blocked the arrows with his hands and body. Arrow after arrow hit him, but he didn't move. He stayed strong, protecting the Prophet.

One arrow was about to hit the Prophet's face, but Talha put his hand up and caught it! His hand was badly injured, and it would never work properly again. But Talha didn't care - he had saved the Prophet's life.

By the end of the battle, Talha had more than 70 wounds on his body! The Prophet looked at him with tears in his eyes and said, "Talha has earned Paradise today!"

From that day on, people called him "The Living Martyr" because he had been willing to die for the Prophet but Allah kept him alive to continue doing good deeds.

## Lesson Learned: 

True love means being willing to sacrifice yourself for others. When you truly care about someone, you protect them even if it's hard or painful for you.

inspire.title: The Wealthy Man Who Gave It All Away
inspire.content:
Talha was not just brave - he was also a very successful businessman. He worked hard and became very wealthy. But unlike many rich people, Talha never held onto his money tightly.

One day, a big caravan of Talha's arrived from a business trip. It was filled with valuable goods worth 700,000 dirhams - that's like millions of dollars today! It was so much wealth that news spread throughout Madinah.

Talha's wife said to him, "This is a huge amount! What will you do with it?"

Talha smiled and said, "I will spend it all in the way of Allah before this night ends."

His wife was surprised! "All of it? In one night?"

Talha nodded. That very night, he went to every poor family, every widow, every orphan, and every person in need in Madinah. He distributed all the wealth before dawn!

When people asked him, "Don't you want to save some for yourself?", Talha said something beautiful: "I am ashamed to meet Allah while I have more wealth than I need and there are Muslims who are hungry."

By morning, Talha had nothing left from that huge caravan. But his heart was full of joy, and the whole city was smiling because of his generosity.

## Lesson Learned: 

Money is a blessing, but it's meant to be shared. The happiest people are those who use their wealth to make others happy. Don't love money more than you love helping people.

inspire.title: The First Sword Raised for Islam
inspire.content:
Zubair was only 15 years old when he accepted Islam. He was young, but he had the heart of a lion!

One day, a false rumor spread in Makkah that the Prophet Muhammad had been killed. When young Zubair heard this, he didn't cry or hide. Instead, he grabbed his sword and ran through the streets of Makkah, ready to fight anyone who had hurt the Prophet!

People saw this teenage boy running with his sword and were amazed at his bravery. When Zubair found the Prophet safe and sound, the Prophet smiled at him and asked, "Zubair, what were you going to do with that sword?"

Zubair said with determination, "I was going to fight whoever hurt you!"

The Prophet was so touched by this young boy's courage that he hugged him and prayed for him. From that day on, Zubair became known as one of the bravest warriors in Islam.

Zubair was the first person to raise his sword to defend Islam. Even though he was young, he showed that age doesn't matter when you have courage and faith in your heart.

In every battle after that, Zubair was always in the front lines, fighting bravely for Islam. The Prophet loved him so much that he called him "my disciple."

## Lesson Learned: 

You're never too young to be brave and stand up for what's right. True courage comes from the heart, not from age or size.

inspire.title: The Spy Who Risked Everything
inspire.content:
During the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench), the Muslims were surrounded by a huge enemy army. The situation was very scary, and the Muslims needed to know what the enemy was planning.

The Prophet looked at his companions and asked, "Who will go into the enemy camp and bring us news about what they're planning? I promise them Paradise!"

It was a dangerous mission. The enemy camp was full of thousands of armed soldiers, and anyone caught spying would be killed immediately.

Everyone was silent. It was too dangerous! But then Zubair stood up and said, "I will go!"

The Prophet was so happy! But then he asked again, "Who else will go tomorrow night?"

Again, silence. And again, Zubair stood up, "I will go!"

The Prophet asked a third time for the next night. And for the third time, only Zubair volunteered!

Zubair went alone into the enemy camp three nights in a row! Each time, he snuck past thousands of enemy soldiers, gathered information about their plans, and returned safely to tell the Prophet.

The Prophet was amazed by Zubair's courage. He said, "Every Prophet has a special disciple, and Zubair is mine!"

Because of Zubair's bravery, the Muslims knew what the enemy was planning and were able to defend themselves successfully.

## Lesson Learned: 

Real heroes volunteer for dangerous tasks when no one else will. When something needs to be done for a good cause, be the first to step forward, even if it's scary.
