inspire.title: The Man Who Started With Nothing
inspire.content:
Abdulrahman ibn Awf was a wealthy man in Makkah. But when he migrated to Madinah for Islam, he left everything behind and arrived with nothing - no money, no house, nothing!

The Muslims of Madinah were very kind. One companion named Sa'd said to Abdulrahman, "Brother, I have two houses and two businesses. Take half of everything I own!"

But Abdulrahman smiled and said something surprising: "May Allah bless you and your wealth, but I don't need it. Just show me where the market is!"

Sa'd was confused. "The market? What will you do there with no money?"

Abdulrahman said, "I will work and earn!"

So Abdulrahman went to the market with nothing. He started by buying and selling small things, working hard from morning until night. He was honest, fair, and kind to everyone he traded with.

Within a few months, Abdulrahman started making profit! Within a few years, he became one of the richest men in Madinah - richer than he had ever been in Makkah!

But here's the best part: Abdulrahman used his wealth to help others. He gave so much charity that half of the Muslim community was eating from his generosity. He equipped entire armies, fed the poor, and helped anyone in need.

The Prophet said about him, "I have seen Abdulrahman entering Paradise, crawling because of the weight of his charity!"

## Lesson Learned: 

Hard work and honesty lead to success. And when Allah blesses you with wealth, share it with others. Your earnings are blessed when you earn them with good character.

inspire.title: The Caravan That Made Madinah Cry
inspire.content:
One day, a huge caravan of 700 camels entered Madinah. All the camels were loaded with food, clothes, and goods. It was such a massive caravan that the whole city heard about it!

The caravan belonged to Abdulrahman ibn Awf, and everyone thought he would sell these goods and make a huge profit.

But Abdulrahman had a different plan. He called out, "This entire caravan is charity for the poor, the orphans, and the widows of Madinah!"

People couldn't believe it! 700 camels of goods - all for charity? That's like giving away millions and millions of dollars!

The Prophet's wife, Aisha, heard about this incredible generosity. She started to cry tears of joy and said, "Give Abdulrahman the good news of a river in Paradise!"

When people asked Abdulrahman, "How can you give away so much?", he said something beautiful: "I heard the Prophet say that whatever you spend in Allah's way will be returned to you many times over. I tested this with a little, then with more, and it's always true! So now I give with confidence."

Abdulrahman continued to give charity throughout his life. Even after he died, people said, "The ground of Madinah shook from the footsteps of people attending his funeral!" because so many people came to honor this generous man.

## Lesson Learned: 

When you give for Allah's sake, you never lose. What you give always comes back to you in this life or the next. The more you give, the more Allah gives you.

inspire.title: The First Arrow Shot for Islam
inspire.content:
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was one of the youngest companions to accept Islam. He was only 17 years old, but he was very brave and strong.

Sa'd was known as the best archer among all the companions. His arrows never missed their target! The Prophet loved this skill and would always say, "Shoot, Sa'd! May my father and mother be sacrificed for you!"

This was a huge honor because the Prophet never said this to anyone else!

One day, the Muslims were praying secretly in a valley outside Makkah. Suddenly, the enemies of Islam found them and started insulting them and trying to attack them.

The Muslims didn't want to fight, but the enemies kept coming closer. Sa'd picked up a bone from the ground (because he had no weapon) and threw it at the enemies. Then he picked up his bow and shot an arrow at them.

This was the very first arrow ever shot in defense of Islam! The enemies were surprised and backed away.

From that day on, Sa'd became known as a great warrior. In every battle, he would be there with his bow and arrows, defending Islam.

The Prophet was so confident in Sa'd's skills that he once gave him all his arrows in a battle and said, "Here, these are all for you!"

## Lesson Learned: 

Whatever talent Allah gives you - use it to help others and defend what's right. Your skills are gifts meant to be used for good purposes.

inspire.title: The Mother's Test
inspire.content:
Sa'd loved his mother very much. He was always kind to her and took care of her. But when Sa'd accepted Islam, his mother was very upset.

One day, his mother said to him, "Sa'd, leave this new religion or I will stop eating and drinking until I die! Then everyone will blame you!"

Sa'd was shocked! He loved his mother so much, but he also loved Allah and Islam. What should he do?

His mother really did stop eating and drinking. One day passed, then two days. She became very weak, but she still refused to eat unless Sa'd left Islam.

Sa'd went to his mother and said something very brave but also very kind:

"My dear mother, I love you more than anything in this world. But I have to tell you the truth: Even if you had 100 souls and they left your body one by one in front of me, I still would not leave Islam. So please, eat and drink. Or don't eat and drink. It is your choice."

When his mother saw how strong Sa'd's faith was, she realized he would never change. Finally, she started eating again.

Later, Allah sent down verses in the Quran about this situation, teaching all Muslims that we should be kind to our parents, but if they ask us to worship other than Allah, we should not obey them in that.

Sa'd continued to be kind and respectful to his mother for the rest of her life, but he never left his faith.

## Lesson Learned: 

Always respect and love your parents, but never compromise on your faith in Allah. You can be kind and firm at the same time.

inspire.title: The Man Whose House Protected the Prophet
inspire.content:
Sa'eed ibn Zayd was one of the very first people to accept Islam. In fact, he accepted Islam even before the Prophet entered the house of Al-Arqam, where Muslims used to meet secretly!

Sa'eed was married to Fatimah, who was Umar's sister. Both of them became Muslims early and kept it a secret because Umar was very angry at Muslims at that time.

One day, they were in their house reading the Quran when they heard a knock at the door. It was Umar! He had found out they were Muslims and came to hurt them.

Sa'eed wasn't afraid. When Umar pushed Fatimah and she started bleeding, Sa'eed bravely stood in front of Umar and said, "Umar, do what you want! We are Muslims and we will remain Muslims!"

But then something amazing happened - this brave moment helped change Umar's heart! When Umar saw how strong their faith was and read the Quran they were reciting, he decided to become Muslim too!

So in a way, Sa'eed and Fatimah's courage in their own house led to one of Islam's greatest heroes accepting the faith.

Sa'eed fought in all the major battles and was promised Paradise by the Prophet. He was known as one of the Ten Companions who were given the good news of Paradise while they were still alive.

## Lesson Learned: 

Sometimes your courage in standing firm can change other people's hearts. Never be afraid to show your faith, even in difficult situations.

inspire.title: The Prayer That Moved a Mountain
inspire.content:
Sa'eed ibn Zayd was known for having prayers that were always answered by Allah. People said, "When Sa'eed makes dua, Allah accepts it!"

One day, a woman named Arwa did something very wrong. She falsely accused Sa'eed of stealing her land. She told lies about him to the government, trying to get him in trouble.

Sa'eed was innocent, but the woman kept insisting on her false claim. Sa'eed was very upset that someone would lie about him.

Finally, Sa'eed raised his hands to the sky and made a powerful dua: "O Allah, if this woman is lying, then take away her sight and make her die in her own land!"

It was a serious prayer because Sa'eed was truly innocent and had been wronged.

Amazing things happened after that! First, the woman became blind - she lost her sight completely! Then, years later, she was walking in that same piece of land she had lied about, and she fell into a hole and died there!

Everything Sa'eed had prayed for came true because he was truthful and she was lying.

People who saw this were amazed at how Allah answered Sa'eed's prayer. They remembered that the Prophet had promised him Paradise, and they understood that Allah protects those who are honest.

## Lesson Learned: 

Always tell the truth and never lie about others. Allah always knows the truth, and He protects those who are honest. Lying may seem easy, but it always leads to bad endings.

inspire.title: The Most Trustworthy Man
inspire.content:
Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah was so honest and trustworthy that the Prophet gave him a very special title: "Ameen al-Ummah" which means "The Trustworthy One of the Nation."

One day, the Christians from Najran sent a message to the Prophet. They said, "We want to make a peace treaty with you, but please send us someone we can trust completely."

The Prophet thought about all his companions. Then he said, "I will send you the most trustworthy person - Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah!"

When Abu Ubaidah arrived in Najran, even though the people there were not Muslims, they immediately trusted him. Why? Because his face showed honesty, his words were always true, and his actions were always fair.

He never cheated anyone. If he promised something, he kept his promise. If someone gave him money to keep safe, he protected it better than his own money. If he was given a job, he did it perfectly.

Abu Ubaidah was also very humble. Even though the Prophet praised him so much, he never bragged about it. He always worked quietly, helping others without wanting anyone to notice.

Years later, when Abu Ubaidah was leading the Muslim army in Syria, a terrible plague spread through the land. His soldiers wanted him to leave to stay safe, but Abu Ubaidah refused. He said, "I will stay with my people." He ended up catching the plague and dying with his soldiers, showing his loyalty until the very end.

## Lesson Learned: 

Being trustworthy means people can count on you completely. Always keep your promises, be honest, and treat everyone fairly - that's how you earn real respect.

options: The Trustworthy One of the Nation

inspire.title: The Friend Who Pulled Out the Arrows
inspire.content:
During the Battle of Uhud, something terrible happened. The Prophet was injured - two rings from his helmet were pushed deep into his cheek by an enemy's sword. The rings were stuck so deep that they were very painful and dangerous.

All the companions were worried. They wanted to help the Prophet, but they were afraid of hurting him more. The rings needed to be pulled out carefully.

Abu Ubaidah came forward and said, "Let me do it."

He loved the Prophet so much that he couldn't bear to see him in pain. Abu Ubaidah bent down close to the Prophet's face. But instead of using his hands, he used his teeth! He bit onto one of the rings very carefully and pulled it out with his mouth.

The ring came out, but Abu Ubaidah's front tooth fell out from the effort! It was so painful, but Abu Ubaidah didn't care. The Prophet was more important to him than his own tooth.

There was still one more ring stuck in the Prophet's cheek. Again, Abu Ubaidah bent down and used his teeth to pull it out. And again, another one of his front teeth fell out!

Now Abu Ubaidah was standing there with two missing front teeth and blood in his mouth, but he was smiling! The Prophet was safe, and that was all that mattered to him.

People later said, "No one ever looked more beautiful with missing teeth than Abu Ubaidah!" because those missing teeth were a badge of honor showing how much he loved the Prophet.

## Lesson Learned: 

True friendship means putting your friend's needs before your own comfort. When someone you love is in pain, you help them even if it hurts you.

inspire.title: The Boy Who Loved to Learn
inspire.content:
Young Abdullah ibn Abbas was only 13 years old when Prophet Muhammad passed away, but he was known as the smartest boy in Medina. How did he become so wise?

Every day, Abdullah would wake up very early in the morning. While other children were still sleeping, he would go to the homes of the older Companions who had spent time with the Prophet. He would knock on their doors and ask, "Can you please tell me what the Prophet said about this?" or "What did the Prophet do in that situation?"

Sometimes, he would wait outside their homes until they woke up. He was so eager to learn that he didn't mind waiting! The older Companions loved his curiosity and taught him everything they remembered.

One day, someone asked him, "Abdullah, why do you work so hard to learn when you're just a child?"

Abdullah smiled and said, "Knowledge is a treasure that never runs out. The more you learn, the richer you become!"

Because of his hard work, Abdullah grew up to become one of the greatest scholars in Islamic history. People from all over the world came to learn from him.

## Lesson Learned: 

Hard work and curiosity make you wise. Never stop asking questions and learning new things, even when it's difficult.

options: He was curious and eager to learn

inspire.title: The Merchant Who Gave Everything
inspire.content:
Abu Bakr was a rich merchant in Makkah. He had a successful business and a comfortable home. One day, the Prophet Muhammad needed help. The Muslims were preparing for an important journey, and they needed supplies - food, water, camels, and equipment.

The Prophet asked, "Who will help?"

Abu Bakr didn't just bring some of his wealth. He brought EVERYTHING he owned! His family's gold, silver, food, camels - he loaded it all up and brought it to help.

The Prophet was amazed. "Abu Bakr, what did you leave for your family at home?"

Abu Bakr smiled peacefully and said, "I left them Allah and His Messenger. That is enough for us."

His family didn't complain. His children understood that helping others was more important than keeping treasures. And you know what? Allah took care of Abu Bakr's family. They never went hungry, and Abu Bakr remained successful because of his generous heart.

## Lesson Learned: 

True generosity means giving even when it's difficult. When you help others with a sincere heart, Allah will take care of you.

inspire.title: The Strong Man with a Soft Heart
inspire.content:
Umar was the strongest, toughest man in Makkah. He was so strong that people were afraid of him! He had a loud voice and could be very scary when he was angry.

One night, Umar was walking through the streets of Medina as the Caliph (leader). It was very late, and he was checking to make sure everyone was safe. Suddenly, he heard a baby crying inside a small house.

Umar knocked on the door. A tired woman opened it, holding a crying baby.

"Why is your baby crying?" Umar asked gently.

"I'm trying to feed him solid food," she explained, "but he's too young and won't eat it. He wants milk, but I don't have money to buy enough milk."

"But why are you forcing him to eat solid food?" Umar asked, concerned.

The woman sighed, "Because Umar - our leader - only gives government help to children after they stop drinking milk. I need that help to feed my family."

Umar's heart broke. He had made a rule without thinking about how it affected mothers and babies!
That very night, Umar went to the treasury and brought flour, dates, and butter to the woman. He even helped her cook! Then he changed the law immediately so that all babies would receive help from birth.

The strong, tough Umar cried that night. He prayed, "Oh Allah, forgive me for making a rule that hurt this mother and baby."

## Lesson Learned: 

True strength is being kind and admitting when you're wrong. Leaders should listen to people's problems and fix their mistakes quickly.

inspire.title: The Brave Young Girl
inspire.content:
Asma bint Abu Bakr was a brave teenage girl who loved adventure. When Prophet Muhammad had to leave Makkah secretly (because bad people wanted to hurt him), Asma had a very dangerous job.

Her father, Abu Bakr, was hiding with the Prophet in a cave outside the city. The enemies were searching everywhere for them! Asma's job was to bring food and water to them every night without being caught.

Every evening, she would pack food in a basket. But she had a problem - she needed something to tie the basket closed, and she couldn't find any rope!

Do you know what brave Asma did? She tore her belt in half! She used one piece to tie the food basket and kept the other piece for herself. Because of this, she was given a special nickname: "The Girl with Two Belts."

For many nights, Asma walked through the dark, dangerous desert to bring food to the cave. She had to be very quiet and careful so the enemies wouldn't see her. Sometimes she was scared, but she never gave up!

When people asked her later if she was afraid, Asma said, "Yes, I was scared. But helping the Prophet was more important than my fear."

## Lesson Learned: 

Bravery doesn't mean you're never scared. It means doing the right thing even when you ARE scared. Creative solutions can solve big problems!

inspire.title: The Man Who Planted Trees
inspire.content:
There was a Companion who didn't have much money, but he loved to help people in a special way. Whenever he traveled, he would carry date seeds in his pocket.

Every time he stopped to rest, he would plant a few date seeds in the ground. People thought this was strange.

"Why are you planting these trees?" they asked. "It takes many years for date trees to grow. You might never eat from these trees yourself!"

The man smiled and said, "That's okay! I'm not planting them for me. I'm planting them for travelers who will come after me. When they're tired and thirsty in the future, they can sit under the shade and eat fresh dates. Even if I never see these trees grow, I'll be happy knowing I helped someone."

Many years later, those little seeds became big, beautiful trees. Hundreds of travelers rested under their shade and ate their sweet dates. And each time someone enjoyed those trees, the man who planted them received blessings from Allah - even though he had passed away!

## Lesson Learned: 

Think about the future and how you can help people you'll never meet. Good deeds create lasting benefits for others, and Allah rewards you even after you're gone.

inspire.title: The Shepherd Boy Who Wouldn't Lie
inspire.content:
Before Islam, there was a young shepherd boy who took care of sheep for his master. One day, a man approached him while he was alone in the hills with the sheep.

"Young boy," the man said, "I'm very hungry. Can you sell me one of these sheep? Your master will never know. I'll pay you good money!"

The boy looked at the gold coins the man offered. His family was poor, and that money could buy so much! He could say a wolf ate the sheep, and nobody would know...

But the boy shook his head firmly. "These sheep don't belong to me. They belong to my master. I cannot sell what isn't mine."

"But your master isn't here!" the man insisted. "Who will know?"

The boy pointed up to the sky and said with confidence, "Even if my master doesn't know, Allah knows! And I would know. I cannot do something wrong even if nobody else sees me."

The man smiled. He was actually testing the boy's honesty! He was so impressed that he told everyone in the village about this honest shepherd.

Later, when Islam came, this same shepherd boy became a Muslim. His name was Abdullah ibn Umar, and he grew up to be known as one of the most honest and trustworthy men in Islamic history.

## Lesson Learned: 

Real honesty is doing the right thing even when no one is watching. Your character is who you are when you're alone.

options: The sheep didn't belong to him

inspire.title: The Thirsty Dog and Jannah
inspire.content:
## The Man Who Earned Jannah with a Shoe Full of Water

Once upon a time, a man was walking down a dusty road under the hot sun. He was so thirsty! His throat was dry, and he could barely swallow. He looked around desperately for water.

Finally, he found a well! He quickly climbed down into it, drank as much cool water as he needed, and climbed back out feeling much better.

But as soon as he got out, he saw something that made his heart hurt. There was a dog nearby, panting heavily with its tongue hanging out. The poor dog was so thirsty that it was licking the wet mud on the ground, trying to get even a tiny bit of moisture!

The man looked at the dog and thought to himself, "This poor dog is suffering from the same terrible thirst I just had. I must help it!"

So, even though he had already climbed out of the well and was tired, he climbed all the way back down. But how would he bring water up for the dog? He didn't have a bucket!

Then he had an idea - he took off his leather shoe, filled it with water, held it carefully in his mouth, and climbed back up. When he reached the top, he gave the dog the water from his shoe. The dog drank and drank until it was satisfied.

Do you know what happened next?

Allah was so pleased with this man's kindness that He forgave ALL his sins and granted him Jannah (Paradise)! Yes, all because he showed mercy to a thirsty animal!

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told us this amazing story, and the companions asked in surprise, "O Messenger of Allah! Will we be rewarded for being kind to animals too?"

The Prophet ﷺ smiled and said, "There is a reward for serving ANY living being."

## Lessons Learned:

- Even small acts of kindness can lead to Jannah
- Animals have feelings and needs just like us
- When you see someone (even an animal) suffering, help them!
- Allah loves those who show mercy to His creation
- Never think a good deed is too small - it might be the deed that saves you!

**Reminder:** The next time you see a thirsty bird, a hungry cat, or any animal in need, remember this man and his shoe full of water. Your kindness could be your ticket to Jannah! 💚

inspire.title: The Woman and the Dog
inspire.content:
## One Act of Mercy Changed Everything

There once lived a woman who had done many wrong things in her life. She had committed many sins, and people looked down on her. She probably thought Allah would never forgive someone like her.

One extremely hot day, she was walking near a well when she noticed something heartbreaking. A dog was circling around the well, its tongue hanging out, almost dying from thirst. The poor animal was so desperate for water that it could barely stand.

The woman stopped and looked at the suffering dog. Her heart filled with compassion. "I must help this poor creature," she thought.

But she didn't have a bucket or a cup with her. What could she do?

She looked down at her feet and had an idea. She took off one of her shoes, tied it to her head covering, and used it as a rope to lower her shoe into the well. She filled the shoe with water, pulled it back up carefully, and gave the water to the thirsty dog.

The dog drank gratefully, its tail wagging. The woman smiled, happy that she could help.

Little did she know that at that very moment, something miraculous was happening in the heavens. Because of her sincere act of kindness and mercy to that dog, Allah forgave her for ALL her sins!

Yes, you read that right - ALL her sins were forgiven because she showed mercy to one thirsty dog! She would enter Jannah (Paradise) because of her compassion!

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told us this incredible story to teach us something very important: No matter how many mistakes you've made, Allah's mercy is always greater. One sincere act of kindness can wash away a lifetime of sins.

## Lessons Learned:

- Never think you're too sinful for Allah to forgive
- Allah's mercy is unlimited and greater than any sin
- Being kind to animals is a way to earn Allah's forgiveness
- Every creature deserves compassion, no matter how small
- One good deed can change your entire destiny
- It's never too late to do something good

**Reminder:** If a woman with so many sins could be forgiven for being kind to a dog, imagine what Allah will do for you when you show kindness! Never underestimate the power of a merciful heart! 💚

inspire.title: The Cat and Hellfire
inspire.content:
## A Serious Warning About Cruelty

This is a sad story, but it's very important for us to learn from it.

There was once a woman who had a cat. Now, having a cat is a big responsibility - you have to feed it, give it water, and take care of it. But this woman didn't do any of that.

Instead, she did something very cruel. She locked the poor cat in a room or tied it up so it couldn't move freely. She didn't give it any food. She didn't give it any water. And she didn't even let it go outside to hunt for mice or bugs to eat!

Day after day, the cat suffered. It meowed in hunger. It cried in thirst. It grew weaker and weaker. Imagine how scared and hurt that poor little cat must have been!

The cat didn't understand why this was happening. All it wanted was some food and water - basic things every living creature needs. But the woman's heart was so hard that she ignored the cat's suffering until finally, the cat died from starvation and thirst.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told us what happened to this woman: She entered Hellfire because of that cat!

Just ONE act of cruelty to ONE small animal led her to such a terrible punishment. This shows us how seriously Allah takes the treatment of animals. They are His creation too, and when we hurt them without reason, we are doing something that makes Allah very angry.

## Lessons Learned:

- Cruelty to animals is a major sin in Islam
- If you take an animal as a pet, you MUST take care of it properly
- Never hurt or neglect any creature - they feel pain just like you do
- Every animal has the right to food, water, and freedom
- Our actions toward all of Allah's creatures matter, not just humans
- Being responsible means taking care of those who depend on you

**Important Rules for Pet Owners:**
- Feed your pets regularly
- Give them clean water every day
- Never lock them up where they can't move or find food
- If you can't take care of a pet, find it a good home
- Take sick animals to the vet
- Be gentle and kind always

**Reminder:** Animals can't speak our language, but they can feel pain, hunger, and fear. When you have power over any creature, use that power with kindness and mercy. Allah is watching how you treat every living thing! 😢

inspire.title: The Worried Mother Bird
inspire.content:
## The Prophet Who Felt a Bird's Pain

One beautiful day, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was with his companions when they passed by a tree. In that tree was a bird's nest with baby birds inside.

Some of the companions thought it would be fun to take the baby birds and look at them up close. They didn't mean any harm - they were just curious! So they took the chicks from the nest.

But then something happened that they didn't expect.

The mother bird came back and couldn't find her babies! She started flying around the area frantically, flapping her wings, chirping loudly in distress. She was so worried and upset! Where were her babies? Were they safe? She flew back and forth, searching desperately.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ saw the mother bird's distress, and his heart was filled with compassion. He immediately asked, "Who has distressed this bird by taking her chicks?"

When he found out that his companions had taken them, he didn't get angry with them, but he taught them an important lesson. He said gently but firmly: "Return her babies to her."

The companions quickly put the baby birds back in the nest. The mother bird flew back to her chicks, and you could almost see her relief! Her babies were safe again!

This beautiful moment taught everyone there a powerful lesson: Even birds have feelings! Even birds have rights! The Prophet ﷺ cared so much about all of Allah's creatures that he even noticed when one little bird was sad.

## Lessons Learned:

- Animals have feelings and emotions just like humans do
- Mother animals love their babies just like human mothers do
- Never separate baby animals from their mothers
- Being curious is okay, but not if it causes harm or distress
- The Prophet ﷺ was merciful to ALL creatures, not just people
- When we see any creature suffering, we should help

**What This Teaches Us About Being Kind:**
- Don't disturb birds' nests or take eggs
- Don't catch butterflies and keep them in jars
- Don't separate baby animals from their mothers
- Watch animals in nature but don't harm them
- If you see an animal in distress, try to help if you can safely

**Reminder:** If the Prophet ﷺ cared so much about one little bird's feelings, shouldn't we also be careful about how we treat every creature? Remember: mercy to animals is mercy to ourselves! 🕊️💚

inspire.title: The Tired Camel
inspire.content:
## The Camel That Made the Prophet Sad

One day, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was walking when he saw something that made him very upset. There was a camel that looked absolutely exhausted. The poor animal was extremely thin - you could see its bones! It looked weak, tired, and hungry.

The camel had clearly been working too hard without enough food or rest. Its owner had been using it to carry heavy loads and travel long distances, but wasn't taking proper care of it.

When the Prophet ﷺ saw this, his eyes filled with sadness. He felt the camel's pain and suffering. He immediately went to find the owner of the camel.

When he found the owner, the Prophet ﷺ didn't yell or shout, but he spoke with serious concern: "Fear Allah regarding these animals who cannot speak!"

Then he gave clear instructions: "Ride them when they are in good condition, and feed them when they are in good condition."

What did the Prophet ﷺ mean by this? He was teaching that:
- You can only use an animal for work when it's healthy and strong
- You must feed animals properly and keep them in good health
- Just because animals can't talk doesn't mean you can treat them badly
- Allah is watching how you treat animals, and you will be held accountable!

The Prophet ﷺ also taught us: "Fear Allah in your treatment of animals." This means we should remember that Allah sees everything we do to animals, and we will have to answer for it on the Day of Judgment.

## Lessons Learned:

- Working animals must be fed well and kept healthy
- Never overwork or overload animals
- Just because animals can't complain doesn't mean we can mistreat them
- Allah will hold us accountable for how we treat animals
- Being kind to animals is part of our faith
- If you can't properly care for an animal, don't keep it

**Rules for Treating Working Animals:**
- Feed them nutritious food regularly
- Give them plenty of water
- Let them rest when they're tired
- Don't overload them with weight they can't carry
- Provide shelter from extreme heat or cold
- Be gentle, never beat them harshly
- Take care of them when they're sick or old

**Reminder:** Animals work hard to help us. They carry our loads, give us milk, help us travel, and do so much more. The LEAST we can do is treat them with kindness, mercy, and care. Remember - Allah is watching! 🐫💚

inspire.title: A Story About Allah's Mercy and Forgiveness
inspire.content:
Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) told us this amazing story to teach us that it's never too late to say sorry to Allah.

A Man Who Made Terrible Mistakes

Long, long ago, there lived a man who had done something very, very bad. He had killed ninety-nine people. That's a huge number! He was a very bad person who had hurt many others. But one day, something changed in his heart. He started to feel sorry for all the terrible things he had done. He thought, "Can Allah ever forgive someone like me?"

Looking for an Answer

The man decided to find someone wise who could answer his question. He asked around, "Who is the most knowledgeable person I can talk to?" People told him about a monk—a religious man who lived alone and prayed a lot. The man traveled to meet him.

"I have killed ninety-nine people," the man confessed. "Can Allah still forgive me?"

The monk looked at him with shock and said, "No! You've done too much evil. There's no forgiveness for you."

When the man heard this, he became very upset and angry. In his anger, he killed the monk too. Now he had killed one hundred people.

Finding the Right Guide

The man still felt troubled in his heart. He asked again, "Who is truly the most learned person who can help me?"

This time, people directed him to a real scholar—someone who had deep knowledge about Allah's mercy.

The man came to the scholar and said, "I have killed one hundred people. Can Allah forgive me?"

The wise scholar smiled kindly and said, "Yes! Of course Allah can forgive you! Nothing stands between you and Allah's forgiveness. But you must make a change."

The scholar continued, "Leave this evil place where you've been living. Travel to a faraway land where good people live—people who worship Allah and do good deeds. Join them, learn from them, and never come back to your old town because it's a bad place that made you do bad things."

The Journey of Hope

The man's heart filled with hope! He immediately started his journey to the good land. He walked and walked, determined to change his life and become a better person. He traveled for days, getting closer and closer to the land of good people. His heart was full of hope and his intention was pure—he truly wanted to change.

When Death Came

But when the man had traveled exactly halfway between his old town and the new land, something happened. Death came to him suddenly, and he died right there on the road. Now, something very special happened in the heavens that we cannot see...

Two groups of angels came:

The Angels of Mercy said, "This man should come with us to Paradise! Look at his heart—he was truly sorry and was trying to change!"

The Angels of Punishment said, "But wait! This man killed one hundred people! He never did a single good deed in his whole life!"

The angels couldn't agree. They were having a debate!

The Wise Decision

Then Allah sent another angel in the form of a human to help them decide. This angel said, "Here's what we'll do: Measure the distance! Which land is he closer to—his old evil town or the new good land?"

The angels measured carefully. And guess what? Even though the man had only traveled halfway, they found that he was just a tiny bit closer to the good land—the land he was trying to reach!

Because of this, the Angels of Mercy took his soul gently and brought him to Paradise.

Lesson:

It's NEVER too late to say sorry to Allah - No matter what bad things you've done, Allah can forgive you if you're truly sorry
Allah looks at your heart - Allah saw that this man truly wanted to change, and that's what mattered most
Take steps to change - Just feeling sorry isn't enough; we need to actually try to become better, like the man who started traveling to a better place
Allah's mercy is HUGE - Even someone who did terrible things for his whole life was forgiven because he tried to change at the end
Choose good friends and good places - The scholar told him to go to a place with good people, because the people around us help us become better or worse

inspire.title: The Brave Young Believers
inspire.content:
A Story from Surah Al-Kahf About Faith and Allah's Protection

The Brave Young Believers

Once upon a time, there was a group of young friends who loved Allah very much. They believed in worshipping only Allah, the One True God.

But there was a big problem. They lived in a city where everyone worshipped statues made of stone and wood—idols that couldn't see, hear, or help anyone. The king was very cruel and mean to anyone who didn't worship these idols.

The young men were in danger! The king wanted to punish them for believing in Allah.

Running to Safety

The young friends decided to leave everything behind—their homes, their families, their comfortable lives. They had to escape to save their faith!

They ran away together, and even their loyal dog came with them. They found a quiet, hidden cave in the mountains and went inside to hide.

"Here we'll be safe," they said. "We can worship Allah without anyone bothering us."

The Miraculous Sleep

Inside the cool cave, the young men felt tired. They lay down to rest with their dog beside them. But this wasn't an ordinary sleep! Allah made something absolutely amazing happen—He put them into a very, very, VERY long sleep. They slept for 309 years! That's more than three hundred years!

Allah protected them the whole time. The sun never hurt them, their bodies didn't age, and they were perfectly safe. They just kept sleeping peacefully, as if time had stopped.

What We Learn:

Never give up hope - Even when everything seems dark, Allah can change everything
Trust in Allah's protection - When you put your trust in Allah, He takes care of you in amazing ways

inspire.title: The Big Surprise
inspire.content:
The Big Surprise

Inside the cool cave, the young men felt tired. They lay down to rest with their dog beside them. Allah put them into a very long sleep. That's more than three hundred years! Allah protected them the whole time. They just kept sleeping peacefully, as if time had stopped.

One day, after all those years, the young men woke up. They stretched and yawned, thinking they had just taken a short nap!

"How long did we sleep?" one asked.

"Maybe a day? Or just a few hours?" another replied.

Their stomachs were rumbling, so they decided one of them should go to the city to buy food.

"Be very careful!" his friends warned. "The king and his soldiers might catch you!"

Everything Had Changed!

When the young man reached the city, he couldn't believe his eyes. Everything looked SO different! The buildings, the clothes people wore, even the money looked strange and old-fashioned.

When he tried to buy food with his coins, the shopkeeper stared at him in amazement. "Where did you get these ancient coins?" he asked.

People began to gather around, asking questions. That's when the young man realized: "We didn't sleep for one day... we slept for HUNDREDS OF YEARS!"

The Amazing Discovery

But here's the best part: The city had completely changed! The mean king was long gone. The people no longer worshipped idols. Now everyone in the city believed in Allah!

The young men's dream had come true. The world they woke up to was a world of believers! When people heard their incredible story, everyone was amazed at Allah's power and protection.

The young men had been willing to give up everything for their faith in Allah. And Allah protected them in the most miraculous way and brought them to a time when they could live in peace.

What We Learn:

Stand strong in your faith - Even when it's hard, Allah will protect you
Allah's timing is perfect - Sometimes we have to be patient, and Allah will make things better in His own time

Remember: Just like these brave young men, when we hold tight to our faith in Allah, He will always be with us and protect us!

inspire.title: The Woman Who Showed Kindness
inspire.content:
Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) told us this beautiful story to teach us something very important about Allah's mercy.

A Woman and a Thirsty Dog

Long ago, there lived a woman who had made many mistakes in her life. She had done things that were wrong.

One very hot day, this woman was walking in the desert. The sun was burning bright, and everything was dry and dusty. As she walked, she passed by a well—a deep hole in the ground where people got water.

Near the well, she saw a dog. But this wasn't a happy, playful dog. This poor dog was panting heavily—breathing fast with its tongue hanging out. The dog looked so tired and weak. It was desperately thirsty and looked like it might die if it didn't get water soon.

A Kind Heart

When the woman saw the suffering dog, something happened in her heart. She felt sorry for the poor animal. She thought, "This dog is one of Allah's creatures, and it needs help!"

But there was a problem—she didn't have a bucket or a cup to get water from the deep well. What could she do?

Then she had an idea!

A Creative Solution

The woman took off her shoe. Then she untied her head covering (the scarf she wore on her head). She tied her shoe to her head covering to make a rope and bucket!

Carefully, she lowered her shoe down into the well. It filled with cool, fresh water. Then she pulled it back up—very carefully so the water wouldn't spill.

She poured the water out for the thirsty dog to drink.

The dog drank and drank. You could see the relief on the dog's face. The woman had saved its life!

Allah's Amazing Mercy

Now here's the most beautiful part of the story:

Allah forgave ALL of the woman's sins because of this one act of kindness!

Even though she had done wrong things in her life, this one moment of mercy—helping a helpless creature that couldn't even thank her or pay her back—was so precious to Allah that He forgave her completely.

What We Learn:

Every act of kindness matters - Even something as simple as giving water to a thirsty animal is incredibly important to Allah
Allah loves those who show mercy - When we are kind to any of Allah's creatures (people, animals, even insects), Allah loves it
It's never too late to do good - No matter what mistakes we've made before, we can always do something good right now
Animals have feelings too - The dog was suffering, and Allah cared about that. We should be kind to all animals
Small actions can be HUGE in Allah's eyes - This woman didn't build a mosque or give away lots of money. She just gave water to a dog. But Allah loved it so much that He forgave all her sins!

How You Can Be Kind:

Give water to birds on hot days
Feed stray cats or dogs if you see them
Don't hurt insects or animals
Help someone carry heavy things
Share your food with someone who's hungry
Smile at someone who looks sad
Help your parents when they're tired

Remember: Every small act of kindness counts! You never know—one simple good deed might be the one that makes Allah most happy with you.

A Special Reminder

If you ever make mistakes (and everyone does), don't give up! Keep doing good things and being kind. Allah's mercy is so, so big. If He forgave someone because they gave water to a dog, imagine how much He wants to forgive us when we try to be good!

Be kind to everyone and everything—and Allah will be kind to you!

inspire.title: The Orphan Baby
inspire.content:
In the city of Makkah, a special baby was about to be born. His name would be Muhammad, and he would grow up to change the world.

But Muhammad's story began with sadness. His father, Abdullah, died before Muhammad was even born. Baby Muhammad came into the world as an orphan, without ever meeting his father.

When Muhammad was born on a beautiful Monday morning, something wonderful happened. His mother Amina saw a special light, and his grandfather Abdul-Muttalib was so happy that he took the baby to the Kaaba and thanked Allah.

Abdul-Muttalib gave him a special name: "Muhammad," which means "the praised one." This name was very unusual - nobody else in Arabia had this name!

Even though Muhammad didn't have a father, Allah gave him people who loved him. His mother Amina cared for him. His grandfather Abdul-Muttalib was proud of him. And a kind nurse named Barakah (also called Umm Ayman) helped take care of him.

But Allah had an even bigger plan for this little orphan baby. He would grow up to become the best person who ever lived, and Allah would give him the greatest gift of all - the Quran.

## Lesson Learned:

Even when we face difficulties and sadness, Allah has a beautiful plan for us. Sometimes the people who face the hardest challenges become the strongest and most special. Never feel bad if your family is different from others - what matters is having good character and faith in Allah.

inspire.title: The Desert Blessings
inspire.content:
When baby Muhammad was just a few months old, a kind woman named Halimah came to Makkah. She was looking for a baby to take care of in the desert, where the air was fresh and clean.

But nobody wanted to take Muhammad because he was an orphan. They thought orphans couldn't pay them much. Halimah and her husband were the last to choose, and only Muhammad was left.

Halimah felt sorry for the little orphan. She said to her husband, "I don't want to go home empty-handed. Let's take this baby!"

And that's when something amazing happened! As soon as Halimah took baby Muhammad, everything changed. Her donkey, which was old and slow, suddenly became fast and strong. Her camel, which had no milk, suddenly had lots of milk! Even the dry land around her home began to grow green grass.

Halimah and her family had been very poor, but now they had plenty of food. Her animals were healthy and fat while other people's animals were still thin and weak. Everyone in the tribe wondered, "What happened to Halimah? Why is she so blessed now?"

Halimah knew the truth - baby Muhammad was special. Wherever he went, he brought goodness and blessings. She loved him so much that even after two years, she asked his mother if she could keep him longer! Muhammad stayed with her until he was about four or five years old.

## Lesson Learned:

Allah's blessings come in unexpected ways. When we help others, especially those in need, Allah rewards us in ways we never imagined. Halimah helped an orphan child, and Allah filled her life with blessings. Always be kind to those who need help!

inspire.title: Three Losses
inspire.content:
Little Muhammad was only six years old when something very sad happened. His mother, Amina, decided to take him on a journey to Madinah to visit his father's grave and see some relatives.

The journey was long and tiring. On the way back to Makkah, Muhammad's mother became very sick. She died in a place called Abwa, far from home. Now Muhammad had lost both his father and his mother. He was a double orphan.

His kind nurse, Umm Ayman, brought him back to Makkah to his grandfather, Abdul-Muttalib. His grandfather loved him very much and took care of him. He would even let young Muhammad sit with him and the leaders of Makkah - something he didn't allow other children to do!

But when Muhammad was eight years old, another sadness came. His dear grandfather Abdul-Muttalib also died. Before he died, he called Muhammad's uncle, Abu Talib, and said, "Please take care of Muhammad. He is special."

So Abu Talib became Muhammad's guardian. Even though Abu Talib wasn't rich, he loved Muhammad like his own son. He would always give Muhammad the best of what he had.

By the age of eight, Muhammad had lost his father, his mother, and his grandfather. But through all this sadness, Allah was teaching him something important: to be kind to orphans and to always help people who are sad or alone.

## Lesson Learned:

Losing loved ones is very hard, but these difficult experiences can make us stronger and more caring. The Prophet Muhammad never forgot what it felt like to be an orphan, which is why he always told Muslims to be extra kind to orphans and those who are alone. When we go through hard times, we learn to understand and help others who are suffering.

inspire.title: The Trustworthy One
inspire.content:
As Muhammad grew up in Makkah, something special about him became clear to everyone: he never lied. Not even once!

While other young people sometimes told lies or broke their promises, Muhammad was different. If he said he would do something, he always did it. If someone gave him something to keep safe, he always returned it exactly as it was.

The people of Makkah noticed this. They started calling him "Al-Amin," which means "The Trustworthy One." They also called him "As-Sadiq," which means "The Truthful One."

If someone needed to travel and wanted someone to keep their valuable things safe, who would they go to? Muhammad! If two people had an argument and needed someone fair to solve it, who would they ask? Muhammad!

Even people who didn't like him or who would later fight against him never said he was a liar. That's how honest he was!

Muhammad never stole anything, never cheated anyone, and never said mean things about people behind their backs. He was gentle and kind to everyone, even animals. He never worshipped the idols that other people worshipped. He knew in his heart that there was only one God.

He kept being honest even when it was hard. Even when people made fun of him for worshipping Allah alone, he still told the truth. Even when people offered him money and power to stop preaching Islam, he refused and stayed true to his message.

## Lesson Learned:

Being honest isn't always easy, but it's always right. When you always tell the truth and keep your promises, people learn to trust you. This trust is more valuable than gold! The Prophet Muhammad showed us that honesty should never change, no matter what. Whether people like us or not, whether it's easy or hard, we should always be truthful.

inspire.title: The Special Wife
inspire.content:
When Muhammad was 25 years old, he worked as a merchant. He was so honest and trustworthy that a wise businesswoman named Khadijah hired him to take her goods to Syria to sell them.

Khadijah sent her servant, Maisarah, to travel with Muhammad and watch over the business. When they came back, Maisarah told Khadijah amazing things: "Muhammad is the most honest man I've ever met. He's kind, truthful, and thinks deeply about everything."

Khadijah was impressed. She was a respected woman of 40 years old, and many rich and powerful men had asked to marry her, but she always said no. But Muhammad was different. He wasn't rich or powerful, but he had something better - excellent character.

Khadijah asked her friend Nafisa to go talk to Muhammad. When Nafisa told Muhammad that Khadijah wanted to marry him, he was very happy and agreed!

They got married, and Khadijah became the first person to believe in Muhammad when he became a Prophet 15 years later. She supported him when everyone else was against him. She comforted him when he was scared and confused after receiving the first revelation.

Together, they had six children: two boys who sadly died young, and four daughters. Muhammad loved Khadijah so much that even after she died, he would remember her kindness and talk about her with love and respect.

## Lesson Learned:

The best marriage partner isn't the richest or most beautiful person - it's someone with good character who supports you and believes in you. Khadijah chose Muhammad because of his honesty and kindness, not because of money. And Muhammad loved Khadijah so much that he never forgot her goodness, even after she passed away. This teaches us to value people for who they are inside, not what they have outside.

inspire.title: The Black Stone
inspire.content:
When Muhammad was 35 years old, the leaders of Makkah decided to rebuild the Kaaba. The old building was damaged and needed repair.

The different tribes of Makkah worked together, each tribe rebuilding one wall. Everything went smoothly until they reached one very important moment: it was time to put the Black Stone back in its special place.

Suddenly, all the leaders started arguing! Each tribe wanted the honor of placing the sacred Black Stone. They argued for four or five days. Some men even pulled out their swords, ready to fight!

Just when a big fight was about to start, the oldest man there had an idea: "Let's wait! Whoever enters the Kaaba first tomorrow morning will decide what to do!"

The next morning, who walked in first? Muhammad! All the leaders saw him and immediately smiled. "It's Al-Amin! The Trustworthy One!" they said. "We will accept whatever he decides!"

Muhammad thought carefully. Then he asked for a large cloth and placed the Black Stone in the middle of it. He said, "Let the leader from each tribe hold one corner of the cloth and lift it together."

They all lifted the cloth until the stone was at the right height. Then Muhammad himself placed the stone in its proper place with his own hands.

Everyone was happy! Muhammad's wise solution meant that all the tribes shared the honor, and no one had to fight. His wisdom saved many lives that day.

## Lesson Learned:

When people disagree, a wise person finds a solution that makes everyone happy. Muhammad didn't choose one side over another - he found a fair way that included everyone. When we face arguments, we should try to find creative solutions that bring people together instead of pushing them apart. Smart thinking can prevent fights and make peace!

inspire.title: The Cave of Light
inspire.content:
When Muhammad turned 40 years old, he started spending a lot of time alone, thinking about life and the world around him. He would go to a quiet cave called Hira on a mountain near Makkah.

In the cave, Muhammad would think about Allah and worship Him. He would look at the stars, the mountains, and the sky, and wonder about who created all of this. He was sad that people in Makkah worshipped statues instead of the One True God.

One night during the month of Ramadan, something incredible happened. Muhammad was alone in the cave when suddenly, an angel appeared in front of him! It was Angel Jibril (Gabriel).

The angel said, "Read!" Muhammad was scared and said, "I cannot read!" The angel hugged him tightly and said again, "Read!" This happened three times, and then the angel said:

"Read in the name of your Lord who created. He created man from a clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous!"

These were the first words of the Quran! Muhammad was so scared and shocked that he ran home to his wife Khadijah, shaking and saying, "Cover me! Cover me!"

Khadijah wrapped him in a blanket and comforted him. When he told her what happened, she said, "Don't worry! Allah will never let you down. You help people, you're honest, and you're kind. This must be something good!"

Khadijah took him to her wise cousin, Waraqa, who told them: "This was the same angel that came to Prophet Moses! You will be a Prophet, Muhammad!"

## Lesson Learned:

Big responsibilities can be scary at first, but Allah only gives us challenges we can handle. When Muhammad felt afraid, his wife believed in him and supported him. We all need people who believe in us when we're scared. And just like Muhammad, when we're honest and kind, Allah will guide us through difficult times.

quiz.question: How old was Muhammad when he received the first revelation?
What was the name of the cave?
What were the first words of the Quran?
options: Read in the name of your Lord
There is no god but Allah

quiz.question: Who comforted Muhammad when he was scared?
What did Waraqa tell Muhammad?

inspire.title: The Secret Message
inspire.content:
After Muhammad became a Prophet, Allah told him to teach Islam quietly at first. For three years, he only told people he trusted about the new message from Allah.

The first person to believe was his wife Khadijah. She believed immediately without any doubt! Then his cousin Ali, who was still a young boy, accepted Islam. After that, his best friend Abu Bakr believed, and then his adopted son Zaid.

Abu Bakr was so excited about Islam that he started telling his close friends about it. He brought many good people to meet Muhammad, and they all became Muslims. These included Uthman, Talha, Zubair, and Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf.

The early Muslims would meet secretly at a house called Dar Al-Arqam. They prayed together and learned about Islam from the Prophet. They had to be careful because if the leaders of Makkah found out, they would be very angry.

During these three years, about 40 people accepted Islam quietly. They came from different families and backgrounds - some were rich, some were poor, some were slaves, and some were free. Islam taught them that all people are equal in front of Allah.

The Prophet taught them how to pray, how to be kind, how to be honest, and how to worship only Allah. They learned that all the statues and idols that people worshipped were just stone and wood - they couldn't help anyone.

These early Muslims had to be very brave. They kept their faith secret because they knew that later, they might have to face danger because of their beliefs.

## Lesson Learned:

Sometimes we have to be patient and careful when starting something new and important. The Prophet didn't rush - he built a strong foundation first with people he could trust. Real change starts small, with dedicated people who truly believe. Also, we learn that Islam values all people equally, no matter if they're rich or poor, young or old.

quiz.question: How long did the Prophet teach Islam secretly?
Who was the first person to accept Islam?
Where did the early Muslims meet secretly?
Who was Muhammad's best friend?
How many people accepted Islam in the first three years?

inspire.title: Calling from the Mountain
inspire.content:
After three years of teaching Islam secretly, Allah commanded Prophet Muhammad to start telling everyone openly. It was time for the whole city of Makkah to hear the message!

One day, Muhammad climbed up Mount Safa in the middle of Makkah and called out, "Ya Sabahah!" This was a special call that people used when there was danger or important news.

People from all the tribes of Makkah came running. "What's wrong? What happened?" they asked.

Muhammad asked them, "If I told you that there was an army behind this mountain ready to attack you, would you believe me?"

Everyone answered, "Yes! Of course we would believe you! You have never lied to us!"

Then Muhammad said, "I am warning you about a severe punishment if you don't worship only Allah! I have been sent as a Prophet to guide you!"

Some people were quiet and started thinking. But his uncle Abu Lahab got very angry and shouted, "May you perish! Did you call us just for this?" He picked up a stone to throw at Muhammad!

Even though people had always trusted Muhammad and called him "Al-Amin" (The Trustworthy), many of them got angry when he told them to stop worshipping idols. They didn't want to change their old ways.

But Muhammad didn't stop. He knew his message was true. He continued to tell people about Allah, even when they got mad at him. He was patient and brave.

## Lesson Learned:

Telling the truth isn't always popular, but it's always right. Even though everyone knew Muhammad never lied, many people still rejected his message because they didn't want to change. This teaches us that some people will disagree with us even when we're right, and that's okay. We should stay true to what we believe is right, just like the Prophet did. Real courage means standing up for truth even when it's difficult.

quiz.question: From which mountain did Muhammad call the people?
What did Muhammad ask the people?
options: If they would believe him about an army
If they would give him money

quiz.question: Who got angry and wanted to throw a stone?
How many years had Islam been taught secretly?
What was Muhammad telling people to do?

inspire.title: The Brave Uncle
inspire.content:
The leaders of Makkah were getting very angry at Muhammad for teaching about Islam. They started hurting the Muslims who had no one to protect them.

One day, a man named Abu Jahl saw Muhammad near the Kaaba and started saying very mean things to him. He insulted the Prophet and said terrible words. Muhammad stayed quiet and just walked away peacefully.

A brave woman who worked for Muhammad's uncle Hamzah saw everything. She was so upset that she ran to find Hamzah, who was returning from hunting with his bow and arrows.

"Hamzah!" she cried, "Abu Jahl said horrible things to your nephew Muhammad, and Muhammad didn't even respond!"

Hamzah was a strong, brave warrior - one of the toughest men in Makkah. He got very angry! He went straight to Abu Jahl, who was sitting with other leaders near the Kaaba.

Hamzah marched up to Abu Jahl and hit him on the head with his bow! "How dare you insult Muhammad!" Hamzah shouted. "I believe in what he believes! I am a Muslim now!"

Everyone was shocked! Hamzah was one of the most respected warriors in Makkah, and now he was protecting the Muslims! Abu Jahl and his friends were too scared to fight Hamzah.

From that day on, Hamzah proudly stood by his nephew and defended Islam. He became known as "Asadullah" - the Lion of Allah. The Muslims felt safer now that they had such a brave protector.

## Lesson Learned:

Standing up for what's right, especially when someone is being treated unfairly, is true bravery. Hamzah could have stayed quiet, but he chose to defend his nephew and accept Islam publicly. Real strength isn't just about muscles - it's about having the courage to protect those who are being hurt and standing up for justice, even when it's scary or unpopular.

quiz.question: What was Hamzah doing when he heard about Abu Jahl insulting Muhammad?
What did Hamzah hit Abu Jahl with?
What did Hamzah say after hitting Abu Jahl?
What was Hamzah known as?
Why did Abu Jahl not fight back?

inspire.title: Umar's Big Change
inspire.content:
There was a very strong and tough man in Makkah named Umar ibn Al-Khattab. He hated Islam so much that he wanted to kill Prophet Muhammad!

One day, Umar grabbed his sword and went out looking for the Prophet, ready to hurt him. On the way, a friend stopped him and said, "Umar! Before you go looking for Muhammad, you should know that your own sister and brother-in-law have become Muslims!"

Umar was shocked and furious! He immediately went to his sister Fatima's house. When he got there, he heard someone reading the Quran in a beautiful voice. He banged on the door angrily!

Inside, they quickly hid the Quran pages they were reading. When Umar burst in, he saw his sister and brother-in-law looking nervous. "I heard you've become Muslims!" he shouted, and he hit his brother-in-law so hard that he bled.

His sister Fatima bravely stood in front of her husband to protect him, and Umar hit her too! Blood started flowing from her face, but she stood strong and said, "Yes, Umar! We are Muslims, and nothing you do will change that!"

Seeing his sister bleeding because of him, Umar suddenly felt terrible. He said, "Show me what you were reading."

Fatima said, "You have to wash yourself first because you're not clean." After he washed, she gave him the pages of the Quran. When Umar started reading, tears began flowing from his eyes. The words were so beautiful and true!

He immediately went to find Prophet Muhammad and said, "I want to become a Muslim!" The Prophet was so happy! Now Islam had two of the strongest men in Makkah protecting it - Hamzah and Umar!

## Lesson Learned:

Even the people who seem most against us can change their hearts. Sometimes the ones who fight against truth the hardest end up becoming its strongest defenders. We should never give up on anyone, and we should never think that someone is too bad to change. Also, when we do something wrong (like Umar hurting his sister), we should have the courage to admit it and change, just like Umar did.

quiz.question: What was Umar planning to do at first?
Who told Umar about his sister being Muslim?
What made Umar change his mind?
Who were the two strongest defenders of Islam?
What did Umar's sister do when he hit her?
options: She stood strong and said she was Muslim

inspire.title: Running Away to Safety
inspire.content:
The leaders of Makkah were being so cruel to the Muslims that Prophet Muhammad had to make a difficult decision. He told some Muslims, "You need to leave Makkah and go somewhere safe."

There was a faraway land called Abyssinia (Ethiopia) ruled by a just Christian king named Negus. The Prophet said, "Go there. The king is fair and won't let anyone hurt you."

About 15 Muslims, including Uthman and his wife Ruqayyah (the Prophet's daughter), secretly prepared to leave. They snuck out of Makkah at night and traveled to the sea, where they found boats to take them across the water to Abyssinia.

When the Quraish leaders discovered the Muslims had left, they were furious! They sent two men with expensive gifts to the king of Abyssinia. They said, "These Muslims are troublemakers! Send them back to us!"

But King Negus was wise. He said, "I must hear from the Muslims first." He called them to his court and asked, "What is this new religion you follow?"

Jafar, the Prophet's cousin, stood up bravely and explained: "We used to worship idols, treat people badly, and do wrong things. Then Allah sent us a Prophet who taught us to worship One God, to be honest, to be kind to neighbors, and to help those in need."

Then Jafar recited verses from the Quran about Prophet Isa (Jesus) and his mother Maryam. When King Negus heard these beautiful words, tears rolled down his face! He said, "This is the truth! These words come from the same God who sent Jesus!"

The king let the Muslims stay safely in his land. The leaders of Makkah had to go back empty-handed. The Muslims lived peacefully in Abyssinia, protected from harm.

## Lesson Learned:

Sometimes we have to leave difficult situations to stay safe, and that's okay. It's not about running away - it's about being smart and protecting ourselves. Also, this story shows us that good people exist everywhere, from all religions and backgrounds. King Negus was a Christian, but he was fair and kind to the Muslims. We should always be fair to everyone, no matter what they believe, just like King Negus was.

quiz.question: Where did the Muslims go for safety?
Who was the king of Abyssinia?

What made the king cry?
What was the king's religion?

inspire.title: The Sad Year
inspire.content:
When Prophet Muhammad was about 50 years old, something very sad happened - the saddest year of his life.

First, his uncle Abu Talib, who had protected him for many years, became very sick. The Prophet loved his uncle so much and wanted him to become Muslim before he died. He sat by his uncle's bedside and gently said, "Uncle, just say 'There is no god but Allah,' and I will be able to defend you on the Day of Judgment!"

But Abu Lahab and other enemies were also in the room. They kept telling Abu Talib, "Don't listen to Muhammad! Stay on the religion of your father!" Sadly, Abu Talib died without accepting Islam. The Prophet was heartbroken.

A few months later, something even worse happened. His beloved wife Khadijah, who had supported him for 25 years, also became very sick and died.

Khadijah had been the first person to believe in him. When he was scared after the first revelation, she comforted him. When everyone rejected him, she supported him. When he felt alone, she was by his side. She used all her money to help Islam. She was his best friend, his partner, and his strongest supporter.

Now both of them were gone - his protective uncle and his loving wife. The Prophet felt so alone. He was so sad that this year became known as "The Year of Grief."

But even in his sadness, the Prophet didn't give up. He knew Allah was with him. He continued to preach Islam and trust in Allah's plan, even though his heart was broken.

## Lesson Learned:

Everyone faces very difficult times in life, even prophets. It's okay to feel sad when we lose people we love. The Prophet cried when Khadijah died - showing emotions and grieving is part of being human. But even in our deepest sadness, we must not give up. The Prophet continued his mission even though he was heartbroken. This teaches us to have faith in Allah during our hardest times.

quiz.question: Who died first in the Year of Grief?
How long had Khadijah been married to the Prophet?
What did the Prophet ask his uncle Abu Talib to say?
options: There is no god but Allah

quiz.question: What was this sad year called?
Did Abu Talib accept Islam before dying?

inspire.title: The Night Journey
inspire.content:
After the Year of Grief, when Prophet Muhammad was feeling very sad and lonely, Allah gave him an amazing gift - a journey like no other!

One night, while Muhammad was sleeping near the Kaaba, Angel Jibril came to him with a special white animal called Al-Buraq. It was faster than lightning! They flew together from Makkah to Jerusalem in an instant.

In Jerusalem, at Masjid Al-Aqsa, something wonderful happened. All the prophets who had come before - Prophet Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and all the others - were waiting there! They all prayed together, and Muhammad led them in prayer. Imagine - leading all of Allah's prophets in prayer!

Then came the most amazing part. Angel Jibril took Muhammad up through the seven heavens! In each heaven, he met different prophets. He saw Prophet Yahya and Prophet Isa in the second heaven. He met Prophet Yusuf in the third heaven. In the fourth heaven, he met Prophet Idris. Prophet Harun was in the fifth, Prophet Musa in the sixth, and Prophet Ibrahim in the seventh heaven!

Finally, Muhammad reached a place so close to Allah that no one had ever been before. Allah spoke to him directly and gave the Muslims a beautiful gift - the five daily prayers! At first, Allah said to pray fifty times a day, but Prophet Musa advised Muhammad to ask for less, knowing it would be hard for people. Allah, in His mercy, reduced it to five prayers, but promised the reward of fifty!

When Muhammad came back and told people about his journey, some didn't believe him. But Abu Bakr, his best friend, said immediately, "If Muhammad said it, then I believe it!" This is why we call him "As-Siddiq" - the one who believes.

## Lesson Learned:

After hardship comes ease. When the Prophet was at his saddest, Allah gave him this special journey to comfort him and honor him. This teaches us that Allah never abandons us in our difficult times. Also, prayer is such a special gift that Allah gave it to us directly! When we pray five times a day, we're doing something that connects us straight to Allah, just like the Prophet did on that amazing night.

quiz.question: What was the name of the special animal that carried the Prophet?
Where did the Prophet go first?
Who immediately believed the Prophet about his journey?
How many daily prayers did Allah originally command?
How many daily prayers do Muslims pray now?

inspire.title: The Promise of Protection
inspire.content:
The Muslims in Makkah were suffering so much. The Prophet needed to find a new place where Muslims could live safely and freely worship Allah.

During the pilgrimage season, six men from a city called Yathrib (which would later be called Madinah) came to Makkah. The Prophet met them and told them about Islam. These men were very excited! They knew that Jews in their city had been talking about a prophet who would come soon.

"This is the prophet the Jews told us about!" they said to each other. "Let's believe in him before they do!" All six men became Muslims and promised to tell their people about Islam when they returned home.

The next year, during pilgrimage season, twelve men from Madinah came. They met the Prophet secretly at night in a place called Aqabah. They made a special promise to the Prophet: "We will worship only Allah, we will not steal, we will not lie, we will not kill our children, and we will obey you in everything that is good."

The Prophet was so happy! He sent one of his companions, Mus'ab ibn Umair, back with them to Madinah to teach people about Islam.

The following year, something even more amazing happened! Seventy-three men and two women from Madinah came for pilgrimage. They met the Prophet secretly at night at Aqabah again. But this time, they made an even bigger promise.

"We will protect you just like we protect our own children and families!" they said. "Come to Madinah, and we will keep you safe!"

This was it! Finally, the Muslims had found a place where they could live in peace. The Prophet gave them permission to start moving to Madinah. A new chapter was beginning!

## Lesson Learned:

Sometimes help comes from unexpected places. The people of Madinah didn't know the Prophet before, but when they heard the truth, they believed and welcomed him. This teaches us to always be open to helping others, even if they're strangers. Also, these people were brave enough to stand up for what's right, even though it meant going against their old ways. Real faith means being ready to help and protect what is true.

quiz.question: What was Madinah called before?
How many men came in the first meeting?
Who did the Prophet send to teach in Madinah?
What did the people of Madinah promise in the second meeting?
How many people came in the third meeting?

inspire.title: The Great Escape
inspire.content:
The leaders of Makkah were furious! Muslims were leaving one by one for Madinah, and they knew if the Prophet left too, Islam would become even stronger.

They held a secret meeting. "We must stop Muhammad!" they said. They came up with an evil plan: one man from each tribe would attack Muhammad at the same time while he slept. This way, everyone would be guilty, and Muhammad's family couldn't take revenge on just one tribe.

But Allah warned the Prophet about their plan! Allah told him it was time to leave Makkah and go to Madinah.

The Prophet had a brilliant plan. He asked his cousin Ali to sleep in his bed that night, wearing his green cloak. The enemies would think it was Muhammad sleeping!

Meanwhile, the Prophet went to Abu Bakr's house. "Get ready, Abu Bakr," he said, "we're leaving for Madinah tonight!" Abu Bakr was so happy he cried! He had been preparing for this moment for months. He even had two camels ready.

That night, while the enemies surrounded his house waiting to attack, the Prophet and Abu Bakr quietly slipped away. Allah made the enemies not see them as they walked right past them!

They didn't head straight to Madinah though - that's what the enemies would expect. Instead, they went in the opposite direction to a cave called Thawr in the mountains.

The people of Makkah were shocked when they found Ali in the bed instead of Muhammad! They were so angry! They sent search parties everywhere, even offering a huge reward (100 camels!) for anyone who could find Muhammad.

The search parties came right to the cave of Thawr! Abu Bakr was terrified. "They're so close!" he whispered. "If they just look down, they'll see us!"

But the Prophet calmly said, "Don't worry, Abu Bakr. Allah is with us."

And then something miraculous happened - a spider quickly made a web across the cave entrance, and a dove made a nest right there! When the searchers came, they said, "No one could have entered here - look at the spider web and bird's nest! Let's search somewhere else."

After three days, when it was safe, the Prophet and Abu Bakr continued their journey to Madinah. After eight days of travel, they finally arrived! The people of Madinah were waiting, singing songs of welcome: "The full moon has risen upon us!"

## Lesson Learned:

When you put your trust in Allah and do your best, Allah will protect you in ways you can't imagine. The Prophet didn't just sit and wait - he made a plan, prepared carefully, and then trusted Allah. That's what we should do too: prepare well, work hard, but always remember that Allah is in control. Also, Abu Bakr showed us what true friendship means - he was ready to risk his life for his friend and his faith.
