What was the name of the cave where they hid?
What made a web across the cave entrance?
How many camels was the reward for finding Muhammad?
What did Abu Bakr say when he was worried?

inspire.title: Building a New Home
inspire.content:
When the Prophet arrived in Madinah, everyone wanted him to stay at their house! People were pulling his camel, saying "Stay with us! Stay with us!"

The Prophet smiled and said, "Let the camel choose!" He let go of the camel's reins, and the camel walked through Madinah until it stopped at an empty piece of land and sat down. "This is where Allah wants me to build," the Prophet said.

The land belonged to two orphan boys. The Prophet wanted to buy it from them fairly, but they wanted to give it to him as a gift! Finally, the Prophet insisted on paying them, because Islam teaches us to be fair in all our dealings.

On this land, the Muslims built the first mosque in Madinah - Masjid An-Nabawi (the Prophet's Mosque). Everyone helped! Rich people and poor people, young and old, all worked together. The Prophet himself carried bricks and stones. While working, the Muslims sang: "This work is not the work of Khaibar, this is more righteous and purer!"

The mosque wasn't fancy. The roof was made of palm leaves, and the pillars were made from palm tree trunks. There were no carpets - just sand on the ground. But it was beautiful because it was built with love and for the sake of Allah.

The Prophet also did something very special in Madinah. He made all the Muslims become brothers! He paired each person from Makkah (called Muhajirun - the migrants) with someone from Madinah (called Ansar - the helpers). 

The Ansar were so generous! They shared their homes, their money, and their date trees with the Muhajirun. Some even offered to give half of everything they owned! The Muslims became like one big family, helping and caring for each other.

The Prophet also wrote a special agreement with the Jewish tribes in Madinah and everyone else living there, promising to live together peacefully and help each other.

## Lesson Learned:

Home isn't just a building - it's where people love and support each other. The Ansar showed incredible generosity by sharing everything with the Muhajirun. This teaches us that being welcoming and generous to others is a beautiful part of Islam. Also, everyone working together to build the mosque, rich and poor side by side, shows us that in Islam, all people are equal when it comes to serving Allah.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet let choose where he would stay?
What was the first mosque in Madinah called?
What were the Muslims from Makkah called?
What were the Muslims from Madinah called?
What was the roof of the mosque made from?

inspire.title: The Day of Furqan
inspire.content:
Two years after moving to Madinah, the Muslims heard that a big caravan from Makkah was coming back from Syria, led by Abu Sufyan. The Muslims went out to meet it, not to fight, but to take back some of the wealth that had been stolen from them when they left Makkah.

But Abu Sufyan heard about the Muslims' plan and quickly sent a message to Makkah: "Help! Send an army!" The leaders of Makkah gathered a huge army of about 1,000 soldiers with 700 camels and 100 horses. They were so confident they would win!

Meanwhile, the Prophet and only 313 Muslims reached a place called Badr. When they saw the huge Makkan army coming, the Muslims became worried. They had so few people, old weapons, and only two horses!

The Prophet gathered everyone for a meeting. "What should we do?" he asked. Abu Bakr and Umar said, "We will fight!" Then Al-Miqdad stood up and said something beautiful: "O Messenger of Allah! Go ahead and we are with you! We will not say what the people of Moses said: 'You and your Lord go and fight!' Rather, we say: 'You and your Lord go and fight, and we will fight with you!'"

The Prophet's face lit up with happiness! Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said, "O Prophet! Even if you take us to the sea and jump in, we will jump with you!"

The night before the battle, it rained. The rain made the ground firm and easy for the Muslims to walk on, but for the Makkans, it made the sand heavy and difficult. The Prophet prayed all night, asking Allah for help: "O Allah! If this small group of Muslims is destroyed today, You will not be worshipped on earth!"

The next morning, the battle began. The Muslims fought with incredible bravery! Allah sent angels to help them! Many of the leaders of Makkah who had hurt the Muslims were killed in this battle, including Abu Jahl, the Prophet's worst enemy.

Against all odds, the Muslims won! With only 313 people, they defeated an army of 1,000! Only 14 Muslims were martyred, but 70 enemies were killed and 70 were captured. The Muslims treated the prisoners with kindness - the Prophet told them to give the prisoners the best food and treat them well.

This battle was so important that Allah called it "Yawm al-Furqan" - the Day when Truth and Falsehood were separated.

## Lesson Learned:

Victory doesn't come from having more soldiers or better weapons - it comes from having faith in Allah and working together. The Muslims won because they trusted in Allah, helped each other, and fought for what was right. Also, even in war, Islam teaches us to be kind and fair. The Prophet showed mercy to the prisoners, which is true strength. When we trust Allah and stay united, He will help us overcome any challenge, no matter how impossible it seems!

quiz.question: How many Muslims fought in the Battle of Badr?
How many enemies came to fight?
Who was the worst enemy killed in this battle?
What did Allah call this day?
How did the Prophet tell Muslims to treat prisoners?

inspire.title: The Test of Uhud
inspire.content:
A year after their defeat at Badr, the people of Makkah wanted revenge. They gathered a massive army of 3,000 soldiers with 700 armor-suited men, 200 horses, and 3,000 camels. They were determined to destroy the Muslims!

When the Prophet heard this huge army was coming, he asked the Muslims in Madinah: "Should we stay in the city and defend it, or should we go out and meet them?" The older, wiser companions said, "Let's stay in the city where we're safe." But the younger Muslims, who hadn't fought at Badr, wanted to show their bravery. "Let's go out and fight them!" they said.

The Prophet decided to listen to the majority and go out. They went to Mount Uhud with 1,000 men. But then something bad happened - Abdullah ibn Ubayy, a hypocrite, took 300 men and went back! Now the Muslims only had 700 people against 3,000!

The Prophet made a smart plan. He put 50 archers on a mountain pass with one clear instruction: "Stay here no matter what happens! Even if you see us winning, don't leave your position!"

At first, the battle was going well for the Muslims! The Makkans started running away. But then the archers made a big mistake. They thought, "The battle is over, let's go get the war booty!" Most of them left their position, even though the Prophet had told them not to.

The Makkan cavalry saw the mountain pass was empty. They came from behind and attacked! The Muslims were now surrounded. In the chaos, a rumor spread: "Muhammad has been killed!" Some Muslims panicked and stopped fighting.

But the Prophet wasn't dead! He was injured - his tooth was broken, his face was cut, and he was bleeding. Ali, Abu Bakr, Umar, and a few brave companions protected him. The Prophet's uncle Hamzah, the Lion of Allah, was martyred in this battle, fighting with incredible bravery.

When the Muslims finally regrouped and the battle ended, they had lost 70 martyrs. The Makkans also lost many soldiers and eventually left. The Muslims were sad and shocked. Why did they lose when they had won at Badr?

Allah sent down verses in the Quran explaining what happened: the Muslims lost because some of them disobeyed the Prophet's command. The archers left their posts for treasure, and this caused the defeat. But Allah also said He forgave them and this was a test to teach them important lessons.

The next day, even though they were tired and injured, the Prophet and the Muslims went after the Makkan army to show they weren't afraid. The Makkans heard this and quickly went back home.

## Lesson Learned:

Obedience to leaders and following instructions is crucial, especially in difficult situations. The archers thought they knew better than the Prophet, and it led to disaster. This teaches us that when we're given clear directions, especially from those with wisdom and authority, we must follow them exactly. Also, this battle taught the Muslims that victory comes only from Allah, not from their own strength. Sometimes Allah tests us with difficulty to teach us humility and important lessons. What matters is that we learn from our mistakes, stay strong in our faith, and keep trying.

quiz.question: How many Muslims fought at Uhud?
How many enemies came to fight?
What was the Prophet's instruction to the archers?
options: Stay in position no matter what

quiz.question: Why did the Muslims lose?
Who was martyred in this battle?

inspire.title: The Big Ditch
inspire.content:
Five years after moving to Madinah, the Muslims faced their biggest threat yet! The Jewish tribes who had broken their promises teamed up with the people of Makkah and other Arab tribes. Together, they formed a massive army of 10,000 soldiers - they called themselves "The Confederates" (Al-Ahzab).

When the Prophet heard this huge army was coming, he called an emergency meeting. "What should we do?" Everyone was worried. Then a Persian companion named Salman Al-Farisi suggested something nobody in Arabia had ever heard of: "In Persia, when we're attacked, we dig a big trench around the city!"

"That's brilliant!" said the Prophet. So all the Muslims - young and old, even the Prophet himself - started digging a huge trench on the north side of Madinah where the enemy would come from. They worked day and night for six days. They were so hungry, many of them tied stones to their stomachs to feel less hunger!

While digging, they hit a very hard rock that no one could break. The Prophet came and struck it with his pickaxe - sparks flew! He struck it again - more sparks! With the third strike, the rock broke into pieces! The Prophet said he saw visions of Muslim victories in Persia, Rome, and Yemen. The Muslims felt hopeful even though they were tired and hungry.

When the massive enemy army arrived, they were shocked! "What is this? Arabs don't fight like this!" They couldn't cross the trench with their horses and camels. For almost a month, they camped outside, occasionally shooting arrows, but they couldn't attack properly.

The Muslims were squeezed between the huge army outside and the traitorous Jewish tribe of Banu Qurayzah inside Madinah who had broken their peace treaty. The situation was so scary that the Quran says: "When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when eyes grew wild and hearts reached to the throats..."

But the Muslims stayed strong! They took turns guarding the trench. Women and children stayed in fortresses for safety. The Prophet kept praying and never gave up hope.

Then Allah sent help in an amazing way! He sent strong, cold winds that blew down the enemies' tents and put out their fires. The enemies couldn't eat hot food or sleep peacefully. They started fighting among themselves. Finally, their leader Abu Sufyan said, "Let's go home! This wind is destroying everything!" 

The massive army of 10,000 broke up and went home without even fighting! The Muslims won without a major battle! The Prophet said happily, "Now we will attack them, and they will not attack us!"

## Lesson Learned:

Sometimes the best solution is a creative one! Salman's idea of digging a trench was completely new to Arabs, but it worked perfectly. This teaches us to be open to new ideas from anywhere and anyone. Also, this battle shows that with patience, smart planning, and trust in Allah, we can overcome huge challenges. The Muslims were outnumbered, hungry, and surrounded by enemies, but they didn't panic. They stayed united, worked hard, and trusted Allah - and He gave them victory without even fighting!

How long did they dig the trench?

inspire.title: The Peace That Seemed Like Defeat
inspire.content:
Six years after Hijrah, the Prophet had a dream. In the dream, he saw himself and the Muslims entering Makkah and performing Umrah (the small pilgrimage). Dreams of prophets are messages from Allah, so the Prophet knew it was time to try to visit the Kaaba!

He announced that they would go to Makkah - not to fight, but to worship! About 1,400 Muslims got ready. They wore simple pilgrim clothes (ihram), took only their travel swords, and brought 70 camels for sacrifice. They wanted to show everyone they came in peace.

When the people of Makkah heard the Muslims were coming, they panicked and sent an army to stop them! But the Prophet didn't want to fight. He took a different, difficult path through rocky mountains to avoid the army.

Finally, they stopped at a place called Hudaybiyyah, just outside Makkah. The Prophet's camel sat down and wouldn't move. People said, "The camel is being stubborn!" But the Prophet said, "No! The same God who stopped the elephant from entering Makkah is stopping us. He has a better plan!"

The leaders of Makkah sent representatives to talk. Finally, they agreed to make a peace treaty. But when the Muslims heard the conditions, they were shocked and upset!

The treaty said:
- The Muslims must go back this year without performing Umrah
- Next year they can come for only three days
- If someone from Makkah joins the Muslims without permission, the Muslims must return them
- But if a Muslim goes to Makkah, they don't have to return them
- There will be peace for ten years

Umar was so upset! "This isn't fair!" he said to Abu Bakr. But Abu Bakr reminded him, "Allah and His Messenger know best."

The Prophet accepted the treaty. As he was signing it, his cousin Ali wrote "Muhammad, Messenger of Allah." The Makkan representative said, "We don't accept that you're a messenger! Write just 'Muhammad son of Abdullah.'" The Prophet told Ali to erase it and change it, even though it hurt to do so.

The Muslims were sad. They felt like they had lost. But as time passed, they realized this was actually a great victory!

Because of the peace:
- People could travel safely and learn about Islam
- In just two years, more people became Muslim than in all the previous years
- The Muslims became stronger and better organized
- Later, one of the treaty's conditions helped them conquer Makkah peacefully!

Allah called this treaty "a clear victory" in the Quran, even though it seemed like defeat at first!

## Lesson Learned:

Sometimes what seems like a loss is actually a blessing in disguise. The Muslims thought they were losing by accepting the treaty, but it turned out to be one of their greatest victories. This teaches us to trust Allah's plan even when we don't understand it. Sometimes we have to be patient and accept things that seem unfair, because Allah knows what we don't know. Also, the Prophet showed us that being flexible and choosing peace over fighting can lead to better results in the long run.

quiz.question: How many Muslims went to Hudaybiyyah?
Why did they go to Makkah?
How long was the peace treaty for?
What did Allah call this treaty in the Quran?
Who was upset about the treaty conditions at first?

inspire.title: The Prophet Writes to Kings
inspire.content:
After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah brought peace, the Prophet decided to send letters to the great kings and emperors of the world, inviting them to Islam!

He sent messengers to six powerful rulers:
1. Heraclius, Emperor of the Roman Empire
2. Khosrau, Emperor of Persia  
3. Negus, King of Abyssinia (Ethiopia)
4. Muqawqas, Ruler of Egypt
5. Mundhir, Governor of Bahrain
6. Harith, King of Damascus

Each letter had the Prophet's seal on it and said something similar: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to [King's name]. I invite you to Islam. Accept Islam and you will be safe. If you refuse, you will bear the sin of your followers."

When the letter reached Heraclius, the Roman Emperor, something interesting happened! He was very curious. He asked if anyone from Muhammad's people was nearby. By chance, Abu Sufyan (who was still not Muslim then) was there with some merchants from Makkah.

Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan many questions: "What is his family background?" "Has anyone in his family claimed prophethood before?" "Do rich people follow him or poor people?" "Do people leave his religion after joining?" "Does he break his promises?" "Have you ever fought him?"

Abu Sufyan (even though he didn't like the Prophet then) had to tell the truth: "He's from a noble family. No one in his family claimed prophethood before. Both rich and poor follow him. People don't leave his religion. He never breaks promises. We fought him and sometimes we won, sometimes he won."

After hearing all this, Heraclius said, "If what you say is true, then he is truly a prophet! He will conquer the place where I stand!" He wanted to accept Islam but was afraid his people would kill him.

Negus, the kind King of Abyssinia, accepted Islam when he received the letter! Muqawqas of Egypt sent beautiful gifts including a lady named Maria who later became the Prophet's wife.

But Khosrau, the proud Persian Emperor, tore up the letter angrily! He said, "How dare someone write to me like this!" When the Prophet heard this, he said, "May Allah tear up his kingdom just as he tore the letter." And years later, that's exactly what happened - the Persian empire fell!

The Prophet had shown that Islam was not just for Arabs - it was a message for all of humanity, from all nations and all backgrounds.

## Lesson Learned:

Islam is for everyone - rich or poor, Arab or non-Arab, king or commoner. The Prophet sent letters to the most powerful people on Earth, showing that he feared only Allah, not any human power. He showed courage and confidence in his mission. Also, this story teaches us that our reaction to the truth matters. Heraclius understood but was too afraid to act. Negus accepted with an open heart. Khosrau rejected with arrogance. When we hear the truth, we should have the courage to accept it, no matter what others think.

quiz.question: How many kings did the Prophet send letters to?
Who was the Roman Emperor?
Who tore up the Prophet's letter?

Who was afraid to accept Islam because of his people?

inspire.title: The Fortress Falls
inspire.content:
After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Muslims went to deal with the Jews of Khaybar who had been plotting against them. Khaybar was a city with massive stone fortresses built on mountains - it looked impossible to conquer!

The Muslims camped outside Khaybar. Every day, they tried to break into the fortresses, but it was so difficult! One fortress in particular, called Qamus, seemed unbeatable.

The Prophet said, "Tomorrow I will give the flag to someone who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him! Through him, Allah will give us victory!"

All night, the companions wondered, "Who will it be?" Everyone hoped it would be them! The next morning, the Prophet called out: "Where is Ali?"

They said, "O Messenger of Allah! Ali is sick. His eyes are hurting him so badly he can barely see."

The Prophet called for Ali anyway. When Ali came, the Prophet put his blessed saliva on Ali's eyes and prayed for him. Immediately, Ali's eyes were healed completely, as if nothing had been wrong!

The Prophet gave Ali the flag and said, "Go with Allah's blessings." Ali went forward with amazing courage. At the gate of Qamus fortress, a huge champion named Marhab came out, challenging anyone to fight him. He was known as the strongest warrior in Khaybar!

Ali stepped forward. They fought, and with one powerful strike, Ali's sword cut through Marhab's shield and helmet! The fortress gate was locked, so Ali grabbed the heavy gate, pulled it off its hinges, and used it as a shield! After the Muslims entered, Ali threw the gate aside. Later, eight men tried to lift that gate and couldn't!

The Muslims conquered fortress after fortress. The Jews of Khaybar were amazed at the Muslims' bravery. Finally, they agreed to surrender. The Prophet made a peace deal with them: they could keep living there and farming, but they had to give half of their crops to the Muslims as tribute.

Something sweet happened after this victory. The Prophet married Safiyyah, the daughter of one of the Jewish leaders. She chose to become Muslim and married the Prophet, showing that Islam was about unity and peace, not revenge.

## Lesson Learned:

Real strength comes from faith in Allah, not from big muscles or stone fortresses. Ali was sick, but when the Prophet prayed for him and gave him the mission, Allah gave him incredible strength. This teaches us that with Allah's help, we can overcome obstacles that seem impossible. Also, the Prophet showed mercy even in victory by allowing the Jews to stay and keep farming. Islam teaches us to be strong when necessary but merciful when we can. True victory is when we win people's hearts, not just battles.

Who did the Prophet give the flag to?
What was wrong with Ali before the battle?
Who was the strong champion from Khaybar?
What did Ali use as a shield?

inspire.title: Going Home
inspire.content:
Eight years after leaving Makkah as refugees, the Muslims were finally going back - and this time, they would enter as victors!

The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was broken when some allies of Makkah attacked allies of the Muslims. The Prophet decided it was time to take Makkah peacefully, but he wanted to surprise them so there would be no big battle.

He gathered 10,000 Muslims and marched toward Makkah. The Quraish didn't know they were coming! When Abu Sufyan (who still wasn't Muslim) heard about the huge Muslim army approaching, he went to investigate.

In the Muslim camp, Abu Sufyan met his old friend Abbas, the Prophet's uncle. Abbas took him to the Prophet. The Prophet said to Abu Sufyan, "Isn't it time for you to believe that there is no god but Allah?"

Abu Sufyan finally said, "Yes! I testify that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger!" After all these years of fighting against Islam, Abu Sufyan finally accepted the truth!

The Prophet told Abu Sufyan, "Go tell the people of Makkah: Anyone who enters Abu Sufyan's house is safe. Anyone who stays in their own house is safe. Anyone who enters the Masjid Al-Haram (Sacred Mosque) is safe."

As the Muslim army entered Makkah, the Prophet rode his camel with his head bowed low in humility, reciting Surah Al-Fath (The Victory). He wasn't proud or boastful - he was thanking Allah!

The people of Makkah, who had tortured the Muslims for years, were terrified. What would the Prophet do to them? This was his chance for revenge!

The Prophet gathered everyone at the Kaaba. He asked them, "What do you think I will do with you?"

They replied nervously, "You are a noble brother, son of a noble brother."

Then the Prophet said the most beautiful words: "I say to you what Yusuf (Joseph) said to his brothers: 'No blame on you today! Go, you are all free!'"

Everyone was shocked! The Prophet forgave them all! No punishment, no revenge, nothing! Even Hind, who had eaten his uncle Hamzah's liver, was forgiven. Even the poets who made fun of him were forgiven (though later some chose not to accept the forgiveness and left).

Then the Prophet entered the Kaaba. There were 360 idols inside and around it. He pointed at each idol with his stick and recited: "Truth has come and falsehood has vanished!" One by one, all the idols fell down! The House of Allah was purified!

People came in crowds to accept Islam. The city that had forced the Muslims to leave now welcomed them back with open arms. Makkah was finally home again!

## Lesson Learned:

The greatest victory is when we can forgive those who hurt us. The Prophet had every right to punish the people of Makkah, but instead, he chose mercy. This is true strength - being powerful enough to take revenge but choosing forgiveness instead. His mercy and kindness won more hearts than any battle could. This teaches us that when we have the power to hurt someone who hurt us, we should try to forgive instead. Forgiveness is not weakness - it's the strongest thing we can do!

Who finally accepted Islam when the Muslims came?
What did the Prophet say to the people of Makkah?
How many idols were in the Kaaba?
What did the Prophet do to the idols?

inspire.title: When the Muslims Became Proud
inspire.content:
Right after conquering Makkah, the Muslims faced a new challenge! Two powerful tribes, Hawazin and Thaqif, gathered a huge army to fight the Muslims. They brought their women, children, and all their wealth to the battlefield, thinking this would make their men fight harder because they'd be protecting everything they owned.

The Muslim army that went to meet them was massive - 12,000 strong! Some young Muslims looked at their huge numbers and said proudly, "We cannot be defeated today because we are so many!"

This made Allah unhappy. The Muslims were feeling proud of their strength instead of trusting in Allah! They were about to learn a difficult lesson.

The battle began in a valley called Hunayn. The enemy tribes had hidden archers in the rocky mountains on both sides. As the Muslim army entered the valley in the early morning darkness, suddenly arrows rained down on them from all sides! It was a surprise attack!

The Muslims panicked! They started running away in confusion! Only about 100 brave companions stayed with the Prophet, including Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, and Abbas. The Prophet's uncle Abbas had a very loud voice. The Prophet told him, "Call the Muslims back!"

Abbas shouted as loud as he could: "O people of the tree! O people of Al-Aqabah!" (reminding them of their promises to the Prophet). When the Muslims heard this call, they felt ashamed for running away. "We hear you! We are coming!" they shouted back and returned to fight.

The tide of battle turned! The Muslims fought with renewed courage and faith. This time they weren't proud - they were asking Allah for help! They pushed back the enemy and won a great victory!

After the battle, they collected enormous war booty - 24,000 camels, 40,000 sheep, 4,000 ounces of silver, and many prisoners. The Prophet didn't keep any of it for himself. He distributed everything generously among the Muslims.

He gave especially large shares to those who had just become Muslim from Makkah, to help win their hearts completely. This upset some of the Ansar (the helpers from Madinah). They thought, "We've been with the Prophet longer! Why do these new Muslims get more?"

When the Prophet heard this, he gathered the Ansar and spoke to them with love: "O Ansar! Are you upset about worldly things? The other people will go home with sheep and camels, but you will go home with the Prophet of Allah! Isn't that better?"

The Ansar started crying! "Yes, O Messenger of Allah! We are happy with you as our share! That is enough for us!" They realized that being with the Prophet and having his love was worth more than all the wealth in the world!

## Lesson Learned:

Victory comes from Allah, not from our numbers or strength. When the Muslims became proud of how many they were, they were taught a lesson. But when they humbled themselves and asked Allah for help, He gave them victory. This teaches us never to be proud or think we succeed by our own power. We must always remember that everything we have comes from Allah. Also, the Ansar showed us what's truly valuable - having the Prophet's love and being with him was better than any treasure. Real wealth is not money or things, but having good relationships and staying close to what's truly important.

quiz.question: How many Muslims went to the Battle of Hunayn?
Why did some Muslims become proud?
What happened at the beginning of the battle?
Who called the Muslims back?
What did the Ansar say was their share?

inspire.title: The Test of Faith
inspire.content:
The hottest summer Madinah had ever seen! The dates were ripe, the shade was cool, and everyone wanted to stay home and relax. But news came that the Roman Empire was gathering a massive army to attack the Muslims!

The Prophet announced: "We must march to Tabuk to face them!" But this time was different. Usually, the Prophet wouldn't say exactly where they were going, but Tabuk was so far (about 500 miles away in the burning desert) that he told everyone clearly so they could prepare properly.

This was going to be the hardest expedition ever. The journey was long, the weather was scorching hot, the enemy was powerful, and many Muslims didn't have enough money for supplies. It was the ultimate test of faith!

The Prophet encouraged everyone to donate. Uthman gave so generously - providing camels, horses, and money for equipment - that the Prophet said, "Nothing Uthman does after today will harm him!" Abu Bakr brought everything he owned! When the Prophet asked him, "What did you leave for your family?" Abu Bakr said, "Allah and His Messenger!" Umar brought half of his wealth.

Even women donated their jewelry. Poor people came crying, "O Messenger of Allah! We want to go, but we don't have animals to ride or supplies for the journey!" The Prophet had to tell them sadly that he couldn't provide for them. They cried with disappointment!

But three men who had money and could go chose to stay behind without any excuse. Their names were Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah. They thought, "It's too hot. The journey is too hard. Maybe we'll go next time."

The Muslim army of 30,000 marched through the burning desert for many difficult days. When they finally reached Tabuk, they found... no enemy! The Romans had heard about the huge Muslim army and were too afraid to come!

The Muslims stayed in Tabuk for 20 days, showing their strength. Then they returned home victoriously without even fighting! But the real test wasn't the fighting - it was who had enough faith to make the difficult journey.

When they returned to Madinah, the three men who stayed behind came to apologize. They tried to make excuses, but the Prophet knew they were lying. He said, "Go away. I will not speak to you."

For 50 long days, no Muslim was allowed to talk to these three men! They were completely isolated. It was so hard! Ka'b said later, "The whole world felt narrow to me even though it's so wide!" They realized their terrible mistake and prayed constantly for Allah's forgiveness.

Finally, Allah sent down verses in the Quran accepting their repentance! The Prophet called them and said with a huge smile, "Congratulations! Allah has forgiven you!" The three men were so happy they cried tears of joy! They had learned their lesson and never disobeyed again.

## Lesson Learned:

Real faith means doing the right thing even when it's difficult and inconvenient. When the test came, some people showed amazing generosity (like Uthman and Abu Bakr), some showed their dedication (like the poor who cried because they couldn't go), and some failed the test (like the three who stayed behind). This teaches us that being a true Muslim means making sacrifices and doing what's right even when it's uncomfortable. Also, we learn that when we make a mistake, true repentance with sincerity can bring Allah's forgiveness. But we must be honest - making excuses only makes things worse!

What did Uthman donate?

inspire.title: The Last Sermon
inspire.content:
In the tenth year after Hijrah, the Prophet announced that he would perform Hajj. When people heard this, they came from everywhere! They wanted to learn how to do Hajj properly and be with the Prophet. More than 100,000 Muslims gathered!

The Prophet did everything carefully, teaching the Muslims each step. On the 9th day of Dhul-Hijjah, at a place called Arafat, the Prophet gave the most important speech of his life. This was called the Farewell Sermon because it was his last Hajj.

Standing on his camel in front of thousands of people, the Prophet spoke with a powerful voice:

"O People! Listen to me carefully, for I don't know if I will meet you again at this place after this year!"

He taught them the most important lessons:

**About Life:** "Your blood, your property, and your honor are sacred - like this sacred day, in this sacred month, in this sacred city!"

**About Equality:** "All mankind is from Adam and Eve. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a non-Arab have superiority over an Arab. A white person has no superiority over a black person, nor does a black person have superiority over a white person - except by piety and good action!"

**About Women:** "O People! You have rights over your wives, and your wives have rights over you. Treat your women well and be kind to them!"

**About Trust:** "Return what you are trusted with to those who trusted you!"

**About Brotherhood:** "All Muslims are brothers to one another. You are all equal!"

After each point, the Prophet would ask: "Have I delivered the message?" The people would shout: "Yes!" Then he would say: "O Allah! Be my witness!"

Then something amazing happened. Allah sent down a verse of the Quran right there:

"This day I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and have chosen for you Islam as your religion." (Quran 5:3)

When the Prophet heard this verse, tears rolled down his cheeks. Abu Bakr, who was standing nearby, also cried. They understood what this meant - Islam was complete. The Prophet's mission was done. Soon, he would leave this world.

The Prophet raised his finger to the sky and said three times: "O Allah! Have I delivered the message?" Everyone responded: "Yes, you have!" He said: "O Allah! Bear witness!"

After the Hajj, the Prophet returned to Madinah. He had taught the Muslims everything they needed. Islam was complete. His work was done.

## Lesson Learned:

The Prophet's final message reminds us of Islam's most important teachings: equality, justice, kindness, and brotherhood. No matter our color, race, or background, we are all equal in front of Allah. The only thing that makes us better is our good character and actions. These weren't just nice words - they were a complete revolution in how people should treat each other! Even today, these teachings show us how to live with justice and kindness. When we treat everyone equally and with respect, we're following the Prophet's final message to humanity.

Where did the Prophet give his farewell sermon?
What makes one person better than another in Islam?
What verse was revealed during this sermon?
Why was this called the Farewell Sermon?

It was the Prophet's last Hajj

inspire.title: The Final Days
inspire.content:
When the Prophet returned from his farewell Hajj, he lived for only three more months. One night, in the middle of the night, he went to the graveyard called Baqi' and prayed for the people buried there. It was as if he was saying goodbye.

A few days later, he woke up with a terrible headache and fever. His beloved wife Aisha asked him, "My head hurts so much!" The Prophet said, "Rather, my head hurts, O Aisha!" But he was smiling, trying to make her feel better even though he was in pain!

For the next two weeks, the Prophet was very sick. All his wives took turns caring for him, but he asked, "Where will I be tomorrow? Where will I be tomorrow?" They understood - he wanted to be in Aisha's room. His wives kindly agreed.

Even though he was very ill, the Prophet tried to lead prayers. But he was too weak. He asked Abu Bakr to lead the prayers instead. Aisha said, "O Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr is a very soft-hearted man. When he stands in your place, he will cry and not be able to recite properly!" But the Prophet insisted: "Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayers."

One morning, while Abu Bakr was leading the Fajr prayer, the Prophet felt a little better. He lifted the curtain of Aisha's room and looked at the Muslims praying. His face lit up with a beautiful smile! The Muslims were so happy to see him that they almost broke their prayer! Abu Bakr started to step back so the Prophet could lead, but the Prophet gestured to him to continue. The Prophet prayed sitting in his room, following Abu Bakr.

That same day, Monday, the 12th of Rabi' al-Awwal, the Prophet's illness became worse. He was lying with his head in Aisha's lap. He kept raising his finger and looking at the ceiling, saying quietly, "With the highest companion... with the highest companion..."

Then, at noon, with his head still in Aisha's lap, the Prophet took his last breath. The greatest man who ever lived had passed away.

Aisha said later, "Allah allowed me the blessing that the Prophet died in my house, on my day, leaning on my chest, and Allah mixed his saliva with mine at his death." (She was softening dates in her mouth for him because he was too weak to chew.)

When Umar heard the news, he couldn't believe it! He stood up with his sword and said, "The Prophet didn't die! Anyone who says he died, I will strike with this sword!" He was in shock - he couldn't accept it.

But Abu Bakr, though his heart was breaking, went to Aisha's room. He uncovered the Prophet's face, kissed his forehead, and cried. Then he went out to the people and said:

"O people! If anyone among you worshipped Muhammad, then know that Muhammad is dead. But if anyone worshipped Allah, then know that Allah is Ever-Living and never dies!"

Then he recited the verse: "Muhammad is only a messenger. Messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back?" (Quran 3:144)

Umar later said, "When I heard Abu Bakr recite these verses, my legs could not carry me and I fell down. I knew for certain that the Prophet had died."

The companions cried and cried. The Muslims buried the Prophet in the same spot where he died - in Aisha's room. Today, his grave is still in the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah, where millions visit to send their prayers and salutations.

## Lesson Learned:

Even the greatest person who ever lived was still human and had to die. But what the Prophet taught us lives forever! Abu Bakr reminded everyone that we worship Allah, not the Prophet. People come and go, but Allah is Eternal. The Prophet left us the Quran and his beautiful example (Sunnah) as guides for all time. Though he's gone from this world, his teachings light our way forever. Whenever we follow his example - being kind, honest, patient, and loving - we keep his message alive in our hearts.

In whose room did the Prophet pass away?
What day of the week did the Prophet pass away?
Who couldn't accept that the Prophet died at first?
Who reminded everyone that we worship Allah, not Muhammad?

inspire.title: The Perfect Example
inspire.content:
After the Prophet passed away, the companions continued spreading his message. They never forgot what he taught them - not just with words, but with his beautiful character and actions.

**He was the kindest person:** He would play with children, help his wives with housework, mend his own clothes and shoes, and even race with Aisha! He never hit anyone, never used bad words, and always smiled.

**He was the bravest:** In battles, when everyone else was running away, he stood firm. Umar said, "When the battle got tough, we would take shelter behind the Prophet!"

**He was the most generous:** He would give away everything he had. One time, a man asked him for something and the Prophet gave him a whole valley full of sheep! The man went back to his people and said, "O my people! Accept Islam, for Muhammad gives like one who fears no poverty!"

**He was the most humble:** Even though he was a Prophet, he would milk his own goat, serve himself, and sit on the ground. He said, "I am only a slave. I eat like a slave eats and sit like a slave sits."

**He loved cleanliness:** He would use miswak (tooth stick) regularly, keep his clothes clean, and always smell nice. He said, "Cleanliness is half of faith!"

**He was the best to his family:** He never raised his voice at his wives. He helped them with work. He made them laugh. Aisha said, "He was the best to his family, and when prayer time came, it was as if he didn't know us - he was so focused on Allah!"

**He cared for everyone:** Rich or poor, slave or free, he treated everyone with respect. He would visit sick people, even if they weren't Muslim. He would walk in funerals, help the needy, and stand up when a Jewish funeral passed by, saying, "Is it not a human soul?"

**He taught us balance:** He would pray at night until his feet swelled, but he also told his companions, "Your body has rights over you, your eyes have rights over you, and your family has rights over you!" He fasted, but also ate. He prayed, but also rested. He worshipped, but also laughed and enjoyed good company.

**He was merciful to everyone:** He even prayed for the people who threw stones at him in Taif! When the angel asked if he wanted the mountains crushed on them, he said, "No! I hope Allah will bring from their descendants people who will worship Allah alone!"

**His last words were about others:** On his deathbed, he kept saying, "The prayer, the prayer! And fear Allah in how you treat those whom your right hands possess (servants and slaves)!" Even at the end, he was thinking about us!

The Prophet Muhammad wasn't just a messenger - he was a living example of the Quran. Aisha said, "His character was the Quran." Everything he did showed us how to live the Islamic way.

Allah says in the Quran: "Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah, you have an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day." (Quran 33:21)

Now his example continues through us! Every time we're kind, honest, patient, or generous, we're following in his footsteps. Every time we pray, recite Quran, help someone, or smile at someone, we're keeping his light alive in the world.

His physical body may be gone, but his teachings, his character, and his message live forever in the hearts of Muslims around the world. May Allah's peace and blessings be upon him always!

## Lesson Learned:

The Prophet Muhammad showed us that being a good Muslim isn't just about praying and fasting - it's about how we treat everyone and everything around us! He was kind to his family, fair to his enemies, gentle with children, caring with animals, and respectful to everyone. This is the true Islam! We should try to follow his example in everything we do. When we're kind like he was kind, patient like he was patient, and generous like he was generous, we're truly following his Sunnah. This is how we keep his beautiful legacy alive!

quiz.question: What did Aisha say about the Prophet's character?
What did the Prophet do when children were playing?
When asked for something, what did the Prophet give one man?
What were the Prophet's last words about?
What does the Quran say about the Prophet's example?

inspire.title: The Trip to Taif
inspire.content:
After the sad Year of Grief, the Prophet decided to go to the city of Taif, hoping the people there would listen to his message. Taif was a beautiful city with gardens and cool weather.

The Prophet walked all the way to Taif with his adopted son Zaid. When they arrived, he went to meet the leaders of the city. He explained Islam to them and asked them to help protect the Muslims.

But the leaders of Taif were even worse than the people of Makkah! They laughed at the Prophet and mocked him. They said mean things and refused to listen. One of them even said, "Couldn't Allah find anyone better than you to send as a messenger?"

Then they did something terrible. They told their children and slaves to chase the Prophet and Zaid out of the city! The children started throwing stones at them. The stones hit the Prophet so hard that his feet started bleeding. Zaid tried to protect him with his body and got hurt too.

The Prophet and Zaid ran to an orchard (garden) outside the city. They sat under the shade of a tree, exhausted and hurt. The Prophet was bleeding and in pain, both physically and emotionally.

Then the Prophet raised his hands and made a beautiful du'a (prayer). He didn't curse the people of Taif! Instead, he said:

"O Allah, to You I complain of my weakness, my lack of resources, and my lowliness before the people. O Most Merciful! You are the Lord of the weak, and You are my Lord. To whom do You leave me? If You are not angry with me, then I do not care what happens to me! Your protection is more important to me!"

At that moment, Angel Jibril came down with another angel, the Angel of the Mountains. The angel said, "O Muhammad! Allah has heard what your people said to you. If you wish, I can crush them between these two mountains!"

The Prophet immediately said, "No! I hope that Allah will bring from their descendants people who will worship Allah alone and not associate anything with Him!"

Even after all that pain and cruelty, the Prophet still had hope and mercy in his heart! He didn't want revenge - he wanted guidance for them!

On the way back to Makkah, something nice happened. A Christian slave named Addas brought the Prophet some grapes from the orchard. When the Prophet said "Bismillah" (In the name of Allah) before eating, Addas was surprised. "This is not what the people here say!" he exclaimed.

The Prophet asked where he was from. "From Nineveh," Addas replied. The Prophet smiled and said, "From the city of the righteous man Yunus (Jonah), son of Matta!" Addas was amazed! He kissed the Prophet's hands and feet, and believed in him!

## Lesson Learned:

The Prophet showed us what true patience and mercy look like. When people hurt him badly, he prayed for them instead of cursing them! He hoped they would be guided, not punished. This teaches us to never give up hope in people, even when they treat us badly. Also, we should pray when we're in difficulty, just like the Prophet did. Allah always hears our prayers. And look - even in this difficult trip, one good person (Addas) believed! Sometimes we have to go through hard times before we see the good results.

quiz.question: Why did the Prophet go to Taif?
options: To hope people would accept Islam

quiz.question: Who went with the Prophet to Taif?
What did the children of Taif do?
What did the Angel of Mountains offer to do?
Who was Addas?

inspire.title: The First Muezzin
inspire.content:
In the early days of Islam in Makkah, there was a slave named Bilal. He was from Abyssinia (Ethiopia) and had dark skin. His master, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, was one of the cruelest men in Makkah.

When Bilal heard about Islam and met the Prophet, his heart filled with faith. He secretly became a Muslim. But one day, his master found out!

Umayyah was furious! He took Bilal out into the hot desert at noon when the sun was burning. He made Bilal lie on the scorching sand and put a huge heavy rock on his chest! The sand was so hot it could burn skin, and the rock was so heavy Bilal could barely breathe.

"Give up your religion!" Umayyah shouted. "Say there are many gods!"

But Bilal, even under torture, kept saying: "Ahad, Ahad!" (One, One!) - meaning there is only One God!

This torture went on for many days. Every day, they would take him out and torture him, but Bilal never gave up his faith!

One day, Abu Bakr was passing by and saw this horrible scene. He couldn't bear it! He went to Umayyah and said, "Fear Allah! How long will you torture this poor man?"

Umayyah mockingly said, "You care so much? Then buy him!"

Abu Bakr immediately bought Bilal and set him free! Bilal was now a free Muslim, and he never forgot Abu Bakr's kindness.

Years later, after the Muslims migrated to Madinah, they needed someone to call people for prayer. The Prophet had a dream where he saw the adhan (call to prayer) being called. When he woke up, Umar came and said he had the same dream!

The Prophet asked, "Who should call the Muslims to prayer?" Someone suggested Bilal because he had the most beautiful, loud voice!

The Prophet called Bilal and taught him the words of the adhan. Then he said, "Stand up, Bilal, and call!"

Bilal stood on the roof of the mosque and called out for the first time:

"Allahu Akbar! Allahu Akbar! (Allah is the Greatest!)
Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah! (I testify there is no god but Allah!)
Ash-hadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah! (I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah!)
Hayya 'ala as-salah! (Come to prayer!)
Hayya 'ala al-falah! (Come to success!)
Allahu Akbar! Allahu Akbar!
La ilaha illa Allah! (There is no god but Allah!)"

His powerful, beautiful voice echoed through Madinah! Everyone rushed to the mosque for prayer. The Prophet smiled with joy!

Later, when Makkah was conquered, the Prophet asked Bilal to climb on top of the Kaaba and give the adhan! Bilal - the former slave who was tortured for his faith - was now calling the adhan from the holiest place in Islam! Some of the old enemies who used to torture him heard his voice and felt ashamed.

Bilal loved the Prophet so much that after the Prophet passed away, Bilal said he couldn't give the adhan anymore. It made him too sad to remember his beloved Prophet. He moved to Syria and lived there until he died.

## Lesson Learned:

Allah doesn't look at our skin color, our wealth, or whether we were born free or slave - He looks at our hearts! Bilal was a black African slave, but his faith was so strong that he became one of the most honored companions. The Prophet gave him the special position of being the first muezzin in Islam! This teaches us that true nobility comes from faith and good character, not from money or family name. Also, Bilal showed us incredible courage - he chose faith over comfort, even when it meant terrible suffering. That's real strength!

inspire.title: The Big Lie
inspire.content:
During one of the expeditions, something very difficult happened to the Prophet's wife, Aisha. The army was returning to Madinah, and Aisha had gone away from the camp to look for her lost necklace. When she came back, she found that the caravan had already left! They hadn't realized she was missing.

Aisha sat down and thought, "They'll notice I'm missing and come back for me." She waited and waited. Eventually, she fell asleep.

A companion named Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, who was traveling behind the army to pick up anything that might have been dropped, found her sleeping there. He recognized her (before hijab rules were established) and was shocked! He brought his camel for her to ride and walked beside it all the way back to Madinah, not saying a word.

When they arrived in Madinah after everyone else, some evil people, especially the hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy, started spreading terrible rumors! They said Aisha had done something wrong! They spread this lie around Madinah.

Aisha didn't know about these rumors at first. She noticed the Prophet was quiet and not as warm as usual, but she didn't know why. When she finally heard what people were saying, she was devastated! She cried and cried! How could people say such terrible lies about her?

The Prophet was also very troubled. He loved Aisha, but these were serious accusations. He asked his companions for advice. Ali said, "O Messenger of Allah, there are many women. Ask her maid; she will tell you the truth."

When they asked the maid Bareerah, she said, "By Allah who sent you with the truth! I have never seen anything wrong with Aisha except that she is young and sometimes falls asleep while watching the dough, and the goat comes and eats it!" (Meaning her only "fault" was being young and innocent!)

But the rumors continued for a whole month! Aisha stayed in her parent's house, crying. The Prophet couldn't receive revelation about this - he had to wait for Allah to tell him what to do. It was a test for everyone.

Finally, one day, the Prophet came to Aisha while she was crying. He sat down and said, "O Aisha, if you have done wrong, repent to Allah. If you are innocent, Allah will declare your innocence."

Aisha stopped crying. She looked at her father Abu Bakr and her mother. They didn't know what to say. Then Aisha, even though she was so young (only 14 or 15), said something amazing:

"By Allah, I will not repent to Allah for something I didn't do! If I say I did it, Allah knows I didn't, and people will believe I'm guilty. If I say I'm innocent, people won't believe me. All I can say is what Prophet Yusuf's father said: 'Beautiful patience! And Allah is the One sought for help!'"

At that very moment, revelation came down! The Prophet's face changed - signs that he was receiving revelation. Then he smiled and said, "Good news, Aisha! Allah has declared your innocence!"

Allah revealed verses in the Quran declaring Aisha completely innocent and punishing those who spread the lie! The main people who spread this slander were punished.

This was such an important event that Allah put it in the Quran forever, defending Aisha's honor!

## Lesson Learned:

This story teaches us many lessons: Never spread rumors or gossip about anyone! Those who spread the lie about Aisha were severely punished by Allah. We should always think the best of people, especially good Muslims. Also, we see that sometimes Allah tests us with difficulties to make us stronger. Aisha showed incredible patience and trust in Allah during this trial. Finally, we learn that truth always comes out eventually. Lies might spread fast, but Allah's justice is certain!

quiz.question: Why was Aisha left behind?
options: She was looking for her lost necklace

quiz.question: Who found Aisha and brought her back?
Who spread the evil rumors?
How long did the rumors continue before Allah cleared her name?
How did Allah clear Aisha's name?
options: By revealing verses in the Quran

inspire.title: Three Years in the Valley
inspire.content:
The leaders of Makkah were getting very frustrated. No matter how much they tortured the Muslims, Islam kept growing! They needed a new plan.

So they made a terrible decision: they would boycott Bani Hashim and Bani Al-Muttalib (the Prophet's family and clan) completely! They wrote an agreement and hung it in the Kaaba. The agreement said:

- No one could marry them or let them marry from other clans
- No one could buy from them or sell to them
- No one could talk to them or sit with them
- This would continue until they handed over Muhammad to be killed!

The Prophet and his family, along with many Muslims, were forced to leave their homes and live in a small valley called Shi'b Abi Talib. This valley had no food, no business, nothing! They were cut off from everything.

Life in the valley was incredibly hard. They ran out of food very quickly. The children would cry from hunger. Sometimes they ate leaves from trees! At night, people outside the valley could hear the sounds of hungry children crying.

The boycott lasted for THREE LONG YEARS! Can you imagine? Three years of hunger, difficulty, and isolation!

The Muslims could only get food during the sacred months when fighting was forbidden. Even then, some kind people would secretly bring them food at night. Abu Talib's wife, Khadijah, spent all her wealth buying food for everyone in the valley, even though she was a rich woman before.

During these three years:
- They ate tree leaves and animal skin when there was no food
- Children grew weak and thin
- The Prophet's wife Khadijah, who used to be wealthy, suffered greatly
- But they never gave up their faith!

Finally, after three years, some good people in Makkah felt ashamed. A man named Hisham ibn Amr felt especially guilty. He secretly went to other decent men and said, "How can we eat and enjoy ourselves while our relatives are starving? This is shameful!"

Five men agreed to end the boycott. They went to the Kaaba where the agreement was hanging. But when they opened it, they found something amazing - termites (small insects) had eaten the paper! The only words left were "In Your Name, O Allah"! The insects had eaten everything else except Allah's name!

This was a miracle! The Prophet had told his uncle Abu Talib this would happen, and it did!

The boycott was over! The Muslims could finally leave the valley and return to normal life. But the three years had taken a toll - many people were weak, and some, including Khadijah, would pass away not long after because of the hardship they endured.

## Lesson Learned:

This story shows us incredible patience and perseverance. The Muslims suffered for three years but didn't give up their faith! Sometimes holding onto what's right means going through very difficult times. But Allah always helps those who are patient. The miracle of the termites eating the agreement showed that Allah was with them all along. Also, we see how Khadijah's wealth, which she used to help the Muslims, was the best use of money - helping people in need and supporting the truth!

Where did the Muslims live during the boycott?
options: In a valley called Shi'b Abi Talib

inspire.title: The Army Without a Leader
inspire.content:
Before the conquest of Makkah, the Prophet sent a messenger named Al-Harith ibn Umair to the ruler of Syria with a letter about Islam. But the governor of the area, Shurahbil ibn Amr Al-Ghassani, did something terrible - he killed the messenger! This had never happened before! Killing messengers was against all rules, even in war!

The Prophet was very upset. Messengers are supposed to be protected! So he decided to send an army to Syria to show that killing messengers would not be tolerated.

He prepared an army of 3,000 Muslims - the biggest army they had sent so far! The Prophet himself didn't go on this expedition. Instead, he appointed leaders carefully:

"Zaid ibn Harithah will be your leader," the Prophet said. "If Zaid is martyred, then Ja'far ibn Abi Talib will lead you. If Ja'far is martyred, then Abdullah ibn Rawahah will lead you."

The Muslims marched toward Syria. When they reached a place called Mu'tah, they got shocking news: the Byzantine Roman Empire had gathered a massive army of 200,000 soldiers to fight them! The Muslims only had 3,000!

The companions held a meeting. "Should we send to the Prophet for reinforcements?" some asked. But Abdullah ibn Rawahah said, "O people! What you dislike is the very thing you came out for - martyrdom! We don't fight with numbers or strength, but with this religion that Allah has honored us with. So move forward!"

They decided to fight despite the overwhelming odds!

The battle began, and it was fierce! The Muslims fought with incredible courage against an army 70 times bigger!

First, Zaid took the flag and fought bravely until he was martyred. Then Ja'far grabbed the flag! He fought so courageously that his right hand was cut off, so he held the flag with his left. When his left hand was cut off too, he hugged the flag to his chest with both arms until he was martyred! They found more than 90 wounds on his body - all from the front, showing he never ran away!

Then Abdullah ibn Rawahah took the flag and also fought until he was martyred!

Now there was no appointed leader! The Muslims were in chaos! In this critical moment, a companion named Thabit grabbed the flag and ran to Khalid ibn Al-Walid (who was new to Islam) and said, "Take the flag, O Abu Sulaiman!"

Khalid said, "No, you take it! You are more worthy!" But Thabit insisted, "Take it! You are better at fighting than me!"

Khalid took the flag and what he did next was amazing! He realized they couldn't win this battle, so he made a brilliant plan to save the Muslim army. He made tactical moves to confuse the enemy and safely withdrew the army back to Madinah! Not by running away in cowardice, but by smart military planning!

When the army returned to Madinah, some children threw dirt at them, calling them cowards. But the Prophet said, "No! They are not those who fled! They are those who will return to fight another day, if Allah wills!"

The Prophet was especially sad about the three martyrs. When he told people that Zaid, Ja'far, and Abdullah were martyred, tears flowed from his eyes. He went to Ja'far's house and held Ja'far's children, crying. Then he said something beautiful:

"I saw them in Paradise! Zaid is there, then Ja'far, who has two wings and flies with the angels, then Abdullah!"

Because of his two wings, Ja'far became known as "Ja'far at-Tayyar" (Ja'far the Flyer)!

## Lesson Learned:

Real bravery isn't about never retreating - sometimes the bravest thing is to save lives by strategic withdrawal, like Khalid did. Also, this battle showed incredible leadership structure - when one leader fell, immediately another took his place. No chaos, no giving up! The three appointed leaders all fought until martyrdom, showing what true leadership means - leading from the front, not from behind. Finally, we learn that those who die for a good cause are not forgotten - they are honored and remembered forever!

inspire.title: Finally Visiting the Kaaba
inspire.content:
Remember the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah? The Muslims had to go back without performing Umrah that year. But the treaty said they could come back the next year for three days!

One year after Hudaybiyyah, it was time! The Prophet announced, "We're going to Makkah to perform Umrah!" About 2,000 Muslims got ready, their hearts full of excitement and longing to see the Kaaba!

They wore their ihram (pilgrimage clothes) and took their swords - not to fight, but for protection, as the treaty allowed. They also brought 60 camels for sacrifice.

The people of Makkah agreed to leave the city for three days, as promised in the treaty. But before they left, they told their servants and slaves: "Watch these Muslims from the mountaintops and tell us everything!"

When the Muslims entered Makkah, it was an emotional moment! Many of them hadn't seen their city or the Kaaba for years! Some cried tears of joy and longing.

The Prophet rode his camel to the Kaaba. He touched the Black Stone with his stick and said "Allahu Akbar!" Then the Muslims performed tawaf (circling the Kaaba seven times). 

The Prophet told the Muslims to run during part of the tawaf to show the watching Makkans that they were strong! The disbelievers had said, "The fever of Madinah has weakened them!" But when they saw the Muslims running and jumping energetically during tawaf, they were amazed! "These are the people we thought were weak?"

For three whole days, the Muslims performed their Umrah rituals with joy and devotion. The Kaaba, which they had been forced to leave, was now in front of them again! They prayed, they made tawaf, they ran between Safa and Marwa, and they offered sacrifices.

During these three days, something else wonderful happened. Khalid ibn Al-Walid, one of the greatest military commanders in Arabia (who had fought against Muslims at Uhud), saw the Muslims and was deeply moved. After the Muslims left Makkah, he traveled to Madinah and accepted Islam! The Prophet was so happy that he said, "All praise is to Allah who has guided you to Islam!"

Also, Amr ibn Al-As, another famous person, accepted Islam around this time!

On the third day, as agreed in the treaty, the leaders of Makkah sent a message: "Time is up! Leave our city!" Even though the Muslims wanted to stay longer, the Prophet respected the treaty and prepared to leave.

Before leaving, something important happened: The Prophet married Maymunah (may Allah be pleased with her), and the Muslims returned to Madinah with happy hearts!

This Umrah was called "The Compensatory Umrah" (Umrat al-Qada) because it made up for the one they couldn't perform the year before.

The Muslims had fulfilled their dreams of visiting the Kaaba, and they had shown the disbelievers their strength and dedication. The trip was a complete success!

## Lesson Learned:

Patience brings beautiful rewards! The Muslims waited a whole year, and then they got to visit the Kaaba with honor and peace. Sometimes Allah delays things not to deny us, but to give us something better at the right time. Also, keeping promises and honoring agreements is so important - even though the Prophet and the Muslims wanted to stay longer, they left when the three days were over because that's what they had agreed to. Keeping your word builds trust and respect, even with enemies!

How many days did they stay in Makkah?
Why did the Prophet tell Muslims to run during tawaf?
Who accepted Islam after seeing this Umrah?
What is this Umrah called?

inspire.title: The City That Closed Its Gates
inspire.content:
After winning the Battle of Hunayn, the Prophet learned that many of the enemy soldiers had run to the city of Taif and locked themselves inside the strong walls. Remember Taif? That was the same city that had thrown stones at the Prophet years ago!

The Muslims marched to Taif and surrounded the city. But conquering Taif was different from other battles - the city had very high, strong walls and lots of food stored inside. The people of Taif refused to come out and fight. They just stayed inside, shooting arrows at the Muslims from the walls!

The Muslims tried many ways to enter the city. They even brought special equipment like catapults (machines that throw rocks) and a siege tower. But nothing worked! The siege lasted for about 15 to 20 days, and some Muslims were hurt by arrows shot from the walls.

The Prophet asked his companions for advice. Some suggested cutting down the grape vineyards and palm trees of Taif to pressure them. The Prophet did order some trees to be cut, hoping it would make the people of Taif come out. But they still wouldn't!

After many days, the Prophet realized this siege could go on for months because Taif had so much food stored inside. He didn't want to keep the Muslims in a long, difficult siege.

So one day, he made an announcement that surprised everyone: "We will leave tomorrow!" 

Some companions said, "But O Messenger of Allah! We haven't conquered Taif yet!" 

The Prophet replied, "Then go and fight tomorrow!"

The next day, the Muslims tried to attack again, but many were wounded by arrows from the walls. So the Prophet said again, "We will leave tomorrow." This time, the companions smiled and obeyed!

Before leaving, someone asked the Prophet, "O Messenger of Allah! Invoke Allah's curse against Taif!" But the Prophet, remembering how they had hurt him years ago and his response then, raised his hands and said:

"O Allah! Guide Taif and bring them to Islam!"

The Muslims left Taif peacefully. They hadn't conquered the city by force, but the Prophet had a different plan - he would win their hearts!

And guess what? The Prophet was right! A year later, the people of Taif saw how Islam was spreading and how good it was. A delegation from Taif came to the Prophet in Madinah and said, "We want to accept Islam!"

The Prophet welcomed them with joy! The same people who had thrown stones at him and fought against him were now coming in peace to accept Islam! The city that wouldn't open its gates when surrounded by an army now opened its heart to Islam!

One of the leaders of Taif, Urwah ibn Mas'ud, became such a devoted Muslim that when he went back to Taif to teach people about Islam, some people got angry and killed him! But his sacrifice helped more people accept Islam.

Soon, the entire city of Taif became Muslim - not by force, but by guidance!

## Lesson Learned:

Sometimes not getting what we want immediately is better in the long run! The Muslims didn't conquer Taif by force, but later the whole city accepted Islam peacefully. This was much better than destroying the city! This teaches us that patience and praying for people's guidance is sometimes better than fighting. The Prophet could have cursed Taif, but he prayed for their guidance instead - and his prayer was answered! Also, we see that time changes people and situations. What seems impossible today might become easy tomorrow. Never give up hope in Allah's wisdom!

quiz.question: Why was Taif difficult to conquer?
How long did the siege last?
What did the Prophet pray for Taif?
Did the Muslims conquer Taif by force?
What happened a year later?

inspire.title: Everyone Wants to Meet the Prophet
inspire.content:
After the conquest of Makkah and the tribe of Hawazin accepting Islam, something amazing happened! Tribes from all over Arabia started coming to Madinah - not to fight, but to learn about Islam and meet the Prophet!

The ninth year after Hijrah became known as "The Year of Delegations" because so many delegations (groups of representatives) came to meet the Prophet!

One by one, tribes that used to worship idols heard about Islam and came to see this Prophet who had united Arabia. They came from Yemen, Bahrain, Oman, and many other places!

**The Delegation of Thaqif:** Remember the people of Taif who threw stones at the Prophet? They sent a delegation to accept Islam! When they came, the Prophet was so kind to them, even though they had hurt him badly years ago.

**The Delegation of Najran:** A group of Christians from Najran came. They were 60 people including priests and scholars. They wanted to discuss religion with the Prophet. For three days, they talked about faith! The Prophet invited them to accept Islam, and some of them did! Those who didn't were still treated with respect and kindness.

**The Delegation of Abdul-Qais:** They came from Bahrain. They were so eager to learn about Islam that they asked many questions. The Prophet taught them the basics of Islam and they left as happy Muslims!

**The Delegation of Bani Hanifa:** When their delegation came, there was a man named Musaylimah among them. He accepted Islam but later became a liar who claimed he was also a prophet! But Allah protected Islam from liars like him.

**The Delegation of Himyar from Yemen:** A big delegation came from Yemen after their leader had already sent a letter accepting Islam. They came to learn more about the religion.

Every delegation that came was treated with honor and hospitality! The Prophet would:
- Welcome them warmly
- Give them a place to stay
- Feed them well
- Teach them about Islam patiently
- Answer all their questions
- Send teachers back with them to teach their tribes

The Prophet would teach each delegation according to their level of understanding. He explained the basics: Tawheed (oneness of Allah), prayer, charity, fasting, and good character.

He would send companions back with these delegations to teach them the Quran and Islam. Some companions like Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari were sent to Yemen as teachers and governors.

People were so impressed by the Prophet's character! His kindness, wisdom, humility, and mercy attracted people to Islam more than anything else. They expected to meet a proud king, but they found a humble servant of Allah who sat on the ground, mended his own clothes, and treated everyone equally!

By the end of this year, most of Arabia had accepted Islam! The religion that started with just one person 23 years ago had now spread across the entire Arabian Peninsula!

## Lesson Learned:

Good character and kind treatment attract people more than force ever could! The Prophet didn't force anyone to accept Islam - people came to him because they saw the truth and beauty in Islam and in his character. This teaches us that the best way to share Islam is through our good behavior, kindness, and patience. When we treat people well, they want to know more about our religion. Also, we see that teaching people according to their level of understanding is important - not everyone needs to learn everything at once. Start with the basics and build from there!

Who came from Taif to accept Islam?
How many Christians came from Najran?
How did the Prophet treat the delegations?
Who did the Prophet send to teach people in Yemen?

inspire.title: The Announcement at Hajj
inspire.content:
In the ninth year after Hijrah, the Hajj season came. The Prophet decided not to go himself that year because some pagans were still performing Hajj the way they used to - including doing tawaf (circling the Kaaba) naked! The Prophet wanted to wait until these old practices were completely stopped.

So he appointed Abu Bakr As-Siddiq to lead the Muslims in Hajj! About 300 Muslims went with Abu Bakr. This was a great honor for Abu Bakr!

After Abu Bakr had already left with the group, Allah revealed important verses in Surah At-Tawbah (Chapter 9) that needed to be announced to all the Arabs at the Hajj gathering. These verses were very important - they were about ending all peace treaties with the idol-worshippers who kept breaking their promises and about final warnings to them.

The Prophet needed someone from his own family to make this announcement (as was the custom). He called Ali ibn Abi Talib and said, "Take these verses and catch up with Abu Bakr. On the Day of Sacrifice at Mina, announce these verses to the people!"

Ali immediately set out on the Prophet's own camel and caught up with the group. When Abu Bakr saw Ali coming, he thought maybe he was being removed from leadership! He asked, "Are you here as a leader or a follower?"

Ali said, "As a follower! The Messenger of Allah has sent me to announce certain verses to the people. You continue as the leader of Hajj!"

Abu Bakr was relieved and happy! They continued together.

On the Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhul-Hijjah), when thousands of Arabs had gathered at Mina, Ali stood up and made this important announcement to all the people:

"O People! I have been sent by the Messenger of Allah to announce to you that:
1. After this year, no idolater shall perform Hajj
2. No one shall do tawaf of the Kaaba naked
3. Those who have treaties with the Prophet have four months to think about their position
4. Anyone who has a treaty, it will be honored until its time ends
5. After four months, there will be no more treaties with idol-worshippers except those who kept their word"

This was a historic moment! Islam was now strong enough to say: "The time for idol worship at the Kaaba is over! This is Allah's house, and only those who worship Allah alone can come here!"

The announcement made it clear:
- Those who wanted to accept Islam had four months to think about it
- Those who had peace treaties and kept them would be honored
- But those who kept breaking treaties and fighting would face consequences

This announcement marked the end of idolatry in Arabia! The message was clear: "Arabia is now a Muslim land. The Kaaba belongs to Allah alone!"

The Muslims performed their Hajj properly and returned to Madinah. The Prophet was very pleased with how Abu Bakr led the Hajj and how Ali delivered the important message.

This was preparing everyone for what would come next year - the Prophet's own Farewell Hajj, where he would deliver his final message to humanity!

## Lesson Learned:

Clear communication and firm boundaries are important! The Prophet made it clear that idol worship at the Kaaba would no longer be tolerated, but he also gave people time (four months) to think and decide. This wasn't cruelty - it was actually mercy, giving people a chance to make the right choice. Also, we see the beautiful relationship between the companions - when Ali came, Abu Bakr didn't get upset or jealous. They worked together for Islam! This teaches us that we should focus on the mission, not on position or ego. What matters is doing what's right, not who gets the credit!

quiz.question: Who did the Prophet appoint to lead Hajj in the 9th year?
Why did the Prophet send Ali after them?
What was being banned at the Kaaba?
How many months were people given to think?
How did Abu Bakr react when Ali came?
options: He was happy to work together

inspire.title: Al-Khwarizmi - The Father of Algebra
inspire.content:
Long ago, before calculators and computers existed, a smart boy named Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi was born. He grew up to become one of the world's greatest mathematicians!
Al-Khwarizmi worked in a special place in Baghdad called the House of Wisdom. Imagine a huge library where the smartest people came to learn and share ideas! The leader, Caliph Al-Ma'mun, built this place because he loved knowledge.
What He Discovered:
Al-Khwarizmi wrote a book about solving math problems step-by-step. The word "algebra" comes from his book's Arabic title! He made math easier by showing people how to solve problems like following a recipe. He also brought us the numbers we use today (0-9), which are much easier than Roman numerals like X, V, and I.
How He Worked:
He was very organized. He broke big problems into small steps and wrote everything clearly so others could learn. He wanted to help ordinary people solve real problems - like dividing land fairly or calculating business deals.
Cool Fact:
The word "algorithm" (used in computers and apps) comes from his name! Every time you use a computer, you're using his ideas from over 1,000 years ago. There's even a moon crater named after him!
His Faith:
Al-Khwarizmi began his algebra book with a prayer to God. He believed that studying math was a way to understand Allah's beautiful creation. He wanted his work to help people and honor God.

quiz.question: Where did Al-Khwarizmi work?
options: In the House of Wisdom in Baghdad

inspire.title: Ibn al-Haytham - The Father of Optics
inspire.content:
Born in Basra, Iraq, Al-Hasan ibn al-Haytham loved asking questions. How do we see? Why does light work this way? What makes rainbows?
He lived during a special time called the Islamic Golden Age when Muslim scientists made amazing discoveries. He read books from many cultures but didn't just believe everything - he tested it himself!
What He Discovered:
Before him, people thought our eyes shot out light rays to see things (like a flashlight!). But Ibn al-Haytham proved the opposite - light bounces off objects and comes INTO our eyes! This was huge! He wrote about this in his famous "Book of Optics."
How He Worked:
He was one of the first to use the scientific method we still use today:

Ask questions
Make a guess (hypothesis)
Do experiments
Write down results
Draw conclusions

He did a famous experiment in a dark room. Light came through a tiny hole and made an upside-down picture on the wall. This proved light travels in straight lines and helped invent the camera!
Cool Facts:
He wrote 96 books! A moon crater AND an asteroid are named "Alhazen" after him. His work helped famous scientists like Leonardo da Vinci and Galileo hundreds of years later.
His Faith:
Ibn al-Haytham was a devoted Muslim. He believed studying nature helped him appreciate God's amazing creation. He said truth should be sought for its own sake. For him, doing science was part of being a good Muslim.

options: That we see with our brains
